Companion to the round-4 design review of issue #4525

Verification votes and corrections, round 4

Every new finding on the round-4 review page was put to three verifiers who tried to refute it (a source-truth lens, a design-text-fairness lens, an intent lens). This page holds their reasons and corrections verbatim. A finding survived when at least two of the three could not refute it. Rejected candidates are listed at the end. The disposition rows of section 3 (one checker plus two re-graders per known item) are here too, under dispo-G.., dispo-H.., dispo-N.., dispo-M.., dispo-F.. and dispo-C.. anchors. The round-1 votes are on their own page, the round-2 votes on theirs and the round-3 votes on theirs.

Partly G08. Forward declarations of bf16, view and const_view should be spelled with the struct key (round 3, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:243 "// h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp: declarations only, no intrinsics. struct bf16; template <typename T, bool aligned, bool dma, typename Dim, typename Stride> struct view; template <typename T, bool aligned, bool dma, typename Dim, typename Stride> struct const_view; template <size_t Rows, size_t Cols> class v_vnni_tensor; template <typename T, size_t Rows, size_t Cols> class v_vnni_view; template <typename T, size_t Cols> class v_vnni_row; ..." design-r4.txt:245 "These declarations are in namespace tron. Use the struct key for the existing bf16, view, and const_view definitions. The new writable native_k_view alias is declared for symmetry. No parent caller requires it. Declare all five view parameters without defaults. Include only the standard headers needed for sizes and integer sequences. The explicit strides avoid depending on a default declared in an intrinsics-bearing header. [S15]" Section 9: design-r4.txt:556 "Spell the existing bf16, view, and const_view forward declarations with struct. Keep the declarations header free of vector-instruction definitions."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked for three things: (a) spell the forward declarations of bf16, view and const_view with the struct key and no default arguments, as h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:17-22 does; (b) do not require including bf16.hpp (forward-declare bf16 instead); (c) drop the writable native_k_view alias or mark it "declared for symmetry; no parent caller uses it". All three are in the body: the block at :243 now gives the declaration text with struct bf16; and the two struct templates, :245 states the struct key and "without defaults", and :245 marks native_k_view as declared for symmetry with no parent caller. The word diff confirms these are round-4 insertions [design-wdiff.txt:140-152]. Facts checked. bf16 is defined as struct bf16 inside namespace tron [h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:10-12]. view is a primary template with five parameters (T, aligned, dma, Dim, Stride = row_major<Dim>) declared with struct [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:22-29]; const_view is forward-declared with the same head and struct [views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:31-36]. Because the fifth parameter is defaulted in views.hpp, a redeclaration must not repeat the default, so "Declare all five view parameters without defaults" is right. The design's two view declarations at :243 match expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:18-22 token for token. The warning context is unchanged: -Wall for GCC or Clang [CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:608-609]. "No parent caller requires it": native_k_view appears only at :243; every parent use (:280, :290, :403, :465) is const_native_k_view. Two notes, no change required. First, the sentence "Use the struct key for the existing bf16, view, and const_view definitions" reads literally as an instruction about the definitions, which already use struct; the block at :243 shows the intended forward declarations, so an implementer cannot build the wrong thing. Second, the source-lens optional sentence (use one key for the new v_vnni_* types in both the forward declaration and the definition) is not in the text; the design consistently shows class for those new types at :243 and :418 and never shows a definition with another key, so the risk is low.

Still needed: Add after :245: 'Define v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view, v_vnni_row and the child's k_vnni_* types with the class key, matching these declarations (the sketch uses class; every type under h/tron/tensor uses struct, and a struct/class mismatch draws clang's -Wmismatched-tags under -Wall).' (J21.)

source re-grader (Resolved): The declarations block now spells struct bf16; template <typename T, bool aligned, bool dma, typename Dim, typename Stride> struct view; and the same for const_view, with five parameters and no defaults [design-r4.txt:243]. The paragraph says "Use the struct key for the existing bf16, view, and const_view definitions", "The new writable native_k_view alias is declared for symmetry. No parent caller requires it." and "Declare all five view parameters without defaults." [design-r4.txt:245]. Facts checked: view is a struct with a fifth parameter defaulted to row_major<Dim> [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:22-27]; const_view is a struct with the same head [:29-34]; bf16 is struct bf16 in namespace tron [h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:10-12]; h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:17-22 forward-declares both templates with struct and no defaults, which the design's block copies. The section-9 row matches the body [design-r4.txt:556]. The checker's quotes exist at :243 and :245. Correction: One optional sentence from the source-lens correction is absent: the design does not say that v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view and v_vnni_row must use the same class-key in kv_cache_fwd.hpp and in v_vnni.hpp. The block declares them with class [design-r4.txt:243]. Both files are new parent code, so a mismatch would be a -Wmismatched-tags warning in the implementer's own code, not a wrong build. Note level only; no status change.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The declarations header now spells the forward declarations with the struct key and no defaults. design-r4.txt:243 has "struct bf16; template <typename T, bool aligned, bool dma, typename Dim, typename Stride> struct view; template <...> struct const_view;". design-r4.txt:245 adds "These declarations are in namespace tron. Use the struct key for the existing bf16, view, and const_view definitions. ... Declare all five view parameters without defaults. Include only the standard headers needed for sizes and integer sequences." Every checkable fact is right: bf16 is a struct [h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:10-12]; view and const_view are struct primary templates whose fifth parameter is defaulted, so a forward declaration must omit the default [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:22-36]; the repository's own forward declarations use exactly this form [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:17-22]. The native_k_view remark the corrected recommendation asked for is present: "The new writable native_k_view alias is declared for symmetry. No parent caller requires it." (design-r4.txt:245). Section 9 at design-r4.txt:556 matches the body. Two notes, no status change: (1) the design does not cite expr.hpp:17-22 as the pattern; the spelled declarations make that reference unnecessary. (2) The source-lens optional sentence "use the same key in kv_cache_fwd.hpp and v_vnni.hpp for v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view and v_vnni_row" is absent; the block declares the three new templates with the class key (design-r4.txt:243), and an implementer who copies the declarations into the definitions keeps the keys matched, so the risk is low. Correction: Minor wording note for the design: "Use the struct key for the existing bf16, view, and const_view definitions" (design-r4.txt:245) can be read as an instruction to edit the existing definitions. The intended meaning, that the forward declarations use the key the existing definitions already use, is unambiguous from the spelled block at :243. Optional rewording: "Forward-declare the existing bf16, view, and const_view with the struct key their definitions use."

Partly G15. fill_random is called a 'poison fill'; it writes finite normal-distribution values (round 3, grade Minor)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:287 "| book::fill_random , fill_storage_slot | Preserve the layout-blind whole-block fill as the explicit test-support exception above. | Keep its random normal-distribution fill and existing lifecycle-test callers. Padding-test NaNs instead come from a NaN source row passed through page::set_v . Do not expose a new public pointer. |" design-r4.txt:468 "| Storage and lifecycle: t_llama_unit , 16-lane build | Retain mixed geometry, EAGLE, allocation failure, release/restore, whole-page and partial-page append, random whole-block fill, and completion cases. ... |" design-r4.txt:275 "- Preserve book::fill_random and its fill_storage_slot helper. This existing test-support operation fills an entire K/V block without interpreting coordinates. It is an explicit exception to the raw-access rule and must not establish readiness. Retain its comment about bypassing partner zeroing. ..." design-r4.txt:58 "| Poison, random fill | ... book::fill_random instead fills blocks from a normal distribution and bypasses partner zeroing. |" design-wdiff.txt:248-250: OLD "poison-fill behavior" NEW "random normal-distribution fill". Section 9: design-r4.txt:554 "Distinguish random finite-value fill from NaN test poison. [Words] [Random fill]" ([Random fill] resolves to #accessors, the anchor above the callers table that holds row :287, per design-r4-links.tsv and the HTML).

Checker assessment: The core defect is fixed: the word "poison" is no longer attached to fill_random, the section-8 lifecycle row says "random whole-block fill" instead of "poison fill", the Words row separates the NaN and 0xa5a5 poisons from the random fill, and the row says test NaNs come through page::set_v with a NaN source row. Facts checked: kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1059 std::normal_distribution<> dis(0.0, 1.0) and :1373 data[i] = static_cast<bf16>(distribution(gen)) (a finite random fill, no NaN); the comment at :1054-1056 says it "bypasses the zero-init V slot invariant"; t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:1919-1925 writes the quiet_NaN row through page->set_v at 16 lanes. design-r4.txt:468 has no "poison" (grep: poison appears only at :58, :317, :443, :463, :554, :604, :638). One concrete part of the corrected recommendation is missing. The recommendation and all three verifier corrections asked the row to name fill_random's two callers, and the source and intent lenses said "existing lifecycle-test callers" is loose because neither caller is a lifecycle test. The row at :287 still says "existing lifecycle-test callers" and names no caller. Source check: git grep fill_random 2880c3aa9b -- t src h shows exactly two book::fill_random callers, t/t_llama_unit.cpp:784-785 inside TEST_CASE("fixed KV layout addresses each slot geometry", "[kv_data][book append]") at :761, and :2008 inside TEST_CASE("apply and join page ranges", "[page_range]") at :1953 (the other fill_random hits are unrelated static helpers in t_dma.cpp, t_mwaitx.cpp and t_topk.cpp). The second caller reads the random values back through page->k(...) and page->get_v(...) at :2026-2041, so the design's omission of "must not be read" is right. Small precision point, optional: the sentence "Padding-test NaNs instead come from a NaN source row passed through page::set_v" holds for the 16-lane branch only. At 8 lanes the same test writes the NaN through page->v(slot, 0, i).set(...) (t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:1924-1925). The round-3 recommendation itself used the set_v-only wording and the design-text lens offered the two-width wording only if both widths must be covered, so this is not graded as a new defect.

Still needed: At :287 replace 'and existing lifecycle-test callers' with 'and its two callers: TEST_CASE fixed KV layout addresses each slot geometry (t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:761, calls at :784-785) and TEST_CASE apply and join page ranges (:1953, call at :2008, which reads the random values back as K and V inputs)'. Optional: 'through page::set_v (16-lane) or page::v().set (8-lane)'.

fairness re-grader (Partly): The terminology defect is fixed. The callers-table row now says "Keep its random normal-distribution fill" instead of "poison-fill behavior" [design-r4.txt:287; design-wdiff.txt:249-250]. The same row adds "Padding-test NaNs instead come from a NaN source row passed through page::set_v" [design-r4.txt:287], which matches the NaN write at t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:1919-1923. Partly G17. Header home of the child's typed K storage operations and of detail::k_vnni_access is not stated; 'k_vnni.hpp' is named without a path (round 3, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:416 "Define k_vnni_tensor, k_vnni_view, and k_vnni_row for the proposed logical expression reads in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp. Move mapping constants, k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, and the existing constexpr free function k_vnni::index there. Keep the function spelling for the independent index checks. Define the typed K store_row, load_row, store_block, token-copy operation, and detail::k_vnni_access in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp. Move their pair_base, pair_row_offsets, and transpose_16x16_epi32 helpers with them. Whole-plane copying uses the defaulted owner assignment described below." design-r4.txt:417 "The cache includes the K tensor header. h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes that header and keeps only qk_group. The cache drops its include of this kernel header. self_attention.hpp includes the kernel header directly for qk_group. Neither tensor header includes an attention kernel header." design-r4.txt:260 "The child defines a separate detail::k_vnni_access in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp ." design-r4.txt:299 "h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp and, in the child, h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp supply definitions." design-r4.txt:102 "Keep each family's access plumbing small." design-r4.txt:434 "In copy_storage_slot , replace the whole-page K memcpy at child kv_cache.hpp:2107 with dst_block.k = src_block.k in the packed branch. Use defaulted owner assignment, as for V. ... Add no K plane-copy helper." design-r4.txt:452 "The mapping, scatter/gather/block-store bodies, plane view, and row expression become local to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp." design-r4.txt:62 "qk_group | The child's AVX-512 query/key score reader in h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp ."

Checker assessment: The lead's final edit item 7 [r3-findings.md:28] asked: name h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp as the home of the typed K bulk operations and of detail::k_vnni_access, move the three detail helpers with them, keep only qk_group in h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp, and write the paths in full at the old :249 and :284. All five parts are in the body. (1) Operations and accessor home: design-r4.txt:416 (new in this revision, design-wdiff.txt:377). (2) Helpers move: :416 names pair_base, pair_row_offsets and transpose_16x16_epi32. Checked against h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb: pair_base at :113 and :119, pair_row_offsets at :126 (namespace detail :109-133), transpose_16x16_epi32 at :153 (detail block from :148). scatter_row (:139-146) calls pair_row_offsets and pair_base at :140 and :144. gather_row (:221-228) calls them at :222 and :225. store_block (:194-216) calls transpose_16x16_epi32 at :204. qk_group (:246-308) calls no detail:: helper. It uses only the constants (TOKEN_BLOCKS_4, BLOCK_TOKENS_16, DIM_STEPS_4, PANEL_ELEMS_512, ROW_ELEMS_32, STEP_PAIRS_16, STEP_DIMS_32, PAIR_2, HEAD_SIZE_128, MAX_KV_MUL_16, BF16_BITS_16, HIGH_HALF_0XFFFF0000) and intrinsics. So 'keeps only qk_group' and 'move their helpers with them' are right. (3) Include graph: :417. The child's kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:27 includes tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp, so 'The cache drops its include of this kernel header' names a real include. The child's self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1-28 does not include tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp directly. It calls k_vnni::qk_group at :1636 and reaches the header through kv_cache.hpp. After the cache drops that include, self_attention.hpp needs a direct include, which :417 orders. Consistent. (4) Paths in full: :260 now says 'in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp' (was 'in its own header'); :299 now names both tensor paths (was 'v_vnni.hpp and later k_vnni.hpp'). The kernel header is named with its path at :62 and :417. (5) Q1 wording: :102 says 'Keep each family's access plumbing small' (round 3 said 'shared', design-r3.txt:95). Fixed as recommended. (6) Plane copy: the recommendation listed 'the plane copy' among the operations to place. The design instead states a choice: no K plane-copy helper; whole-plane copies use the owner's defaulted assignment [:416, :434]. That is a stated option (round-3 G44 applied), and the memcpy site is right: h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2107 memcpy(dst_block.k, src_block.k, sizeof(dst_block.k)) inside copy_storage_slot (:2093-). (7) Not adopted, optional: the design-text verifier's item 5 asked for one sentence limiting detail::k_vnni_access to the typed K operations and the K kernels qk_group and qk_vnni_128x4. The lead's final edit list did not include it. The design lists permitted users for the V accessor at :260 but none for the K accessor. qk_group receives k_vnni_view by value [:434], so it must reach the plane through the accessor. An implementer will infer the V parallel. No change required. Two small notes, no defect: the S18 link '[K storage helpers and operations]' points at h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp#L109-L225 [design-r4-links.tsv:518], while gather_row ends at :228, so the range is 3 lines short. The S10 row [design-r4.txt:661] still describes the child's current kernel header as holding 'address calculations and vector operations'; that is accurate for the saved child head, where they do live there today.

Still needed: Add to :260 after 'The child defines a separate detail::k_vnni_access in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp.': 'Typed K operations and the K-specific kernels qk_group and qk_vnni_128x4 may use it. Page methods, book, and tests do not call it.' (J07 carries the full wording.)

source re-grader (Partly): Five of the six parts of the corrected recommendation are in the body. (1) Line 416 defines the typed K store_row, load_row, store_block, the token-copy operation and detail::k_vnni_access in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp and moves pair_base, pair_row_offsets and transpose_16x16_epi32 with them [design-r4.txt:416]. That is the lead's correction. The three helpers are used only by scatter_row (:140, :144), gather_row (:222, :225) and store_block (:204), and qk_group (:246-308) calls no detail:: helper [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb]. (2) "h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes that header and keeps only qk_group. The cache drops its include of this kernel header" [design-r4.txt:417]. The child's kv_cache.hpp includes the kernel header at :27 today [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:27]. self_attention.hpp calls k_vnni::qk_group at :1636 and includes no k_vnni header itself [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:15-28, :1636], so "self_attention.hpp includes the kernel header directly for qk_group" [design-r4.txt:417] is a correct consequence. (3) The accessor row names the path: "The child defines a separate detail::k_vnni_access in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp" [design-r4.txt:260]. (4) The definitions sentence is path-qualified [design-r4.txt:299], and the Words table names h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp as the child's kernel header [design-r4.txt:62]. (5) Q1 says "Keep each family's access plumbing small" [design-r4.txt:102]. The plane copy is not placed in the tensor header, but the design replaces it with defaulted owner assignment and adds no K plane-copy helper [design-r4.txt:416, :434], the G44 outcome, so that is consistent. Line 452 repeats the destination of the mapping and the scatter/gather/block-store bodies [design-r4.txt:452]. The missing part is the design-text-lens extension: a permitted-user list for detail::k_vnni_access. The V row says who may and may not use v_vnni_access [design-r4.txt:260]. For K the design says only where the accessor is defined [design-r4.txt:260, :416]; "k_vnni_access" appears on no other line. qk_group and qk_vnni_128x4 take k_vnni_view by value [design-r4.txt:434] and need the plane pointer, so an implementer cannot tell whether those kernels may call the accessor. Low risk; one sentence. Correction: Design fix: add one sentence at design-r4.txt:260 or :416: "detail::k_vnni_access may be used only inside the typed K operations and the K-specific kernels qk_group and qk_vnni_128x4." Notes, no change required: the child comment block at h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:655-702 names tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp and the raw functions; the design mentions Note [K VNNI storage] [design-r4.txt:48, :587] but does not say the port updates that header name. The S10 row still says the saved child head defines "address calculations and vector operations" in the kernel header [design-r4.txt:664; design-r4-links.tsv:420]; that describes the pinned source truthfully, and :452 gives the new destination, so it is not a contradiction. Checker evidence quotes are accurate at :416, :417, :260, :299, :102, :434, :452, :62.

fairness re-grader (Partly): Substance present. The corrected recommendation asked the design to (a) put the typed K bulk operations (store_row, load_row, store_block, token copy, plane copy) and detail::k_vnni_access in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp, (b) move the three detail helpers with them, (c) keep only qk_group in h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp, (d) have kv_cache.hpp include the tensor header and drop the kernel include, (e) write the path at the accessor row, (f) write paths at the definitions sentence, (g) change 'shared' to 'each family's', and (h) add one sentence naming who may use detail::k_vnni_access. Items (a)-(g) are done. (a)+(b): design-r4.txt:416 'Define the typed K store_row, load_row, store_block, token-copy operation, and detail::k_vnni_access in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp. Move their pair_base, pair_row_offsets, and transpose_16x16_epi32 helpers with them.' The plane copy is replaced by defaulted owner assignment, stated explicitly at :416 and :434 ('Add no K plane-copy helper'); that is an explicit choice, not an omission. The helper list matches the child: pair_base [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:113, :119], pair_row_offsets [:126], transpose_16x16_epi32 [:153]. (c)+(d): :417 'h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes that header and keeps only qk_group. Design text checked: design-r4.txt:432 "| page::set_k_row , page::get_k_row | Use const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for save and view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for load. The boolean template arguments preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties. Preserve the existing gather/scatter instructions. These K routines do not acquire V's stronger alignment requirement. Wrap scratch without copying. Call typed store_row / load_row . Construct read-only source views explicitly in model save paths, copy paths, and affected test callers. Section 9: :573 "Construct read-only K source views explicitly where deduction cannot apply a conversion. [Typed row operations] [Packed accessors] [K caller migration]".

Checker assessment: The mechanism is now stated and is right. In h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b the rank-1 const_view is final (:361), its pointer constructor is explicit const_view(T const* data = nullptr) (:373-374), and its constructors from view are non-template converting constructors (:382-386). Template argument deduction matches P = const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,...> against the argument type with only derived-to-base and qualification adjustments, so a view or a bf16* argument fails to deduce Aligned and Dma. The rule "construct read-only source views explicitly in model save paths ... and affected test callers" is present. What is missing against the corrected recommendation: all three verifiers and the original recommendation named the callers, and the design names none. The case every verifier called the real gap is not named: kout, the writable slice view returned by row_of (h/tron/models/model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2861-2864), whose .data is passed to set_k_row at :2920, and the raw scratch conv[0] passed at :2924. The test files are not named: t/t_llama_unit.cpp has 32 lines calling set_k_row or get_k_row at 30c4ac82cb, t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp has 8 (for example :401 page->set_k_row(SLOT_0, 0, tok, row.data())), t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp has 1 (:101 zero.data()). The uniform-geometry forwarding overloads at h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1752-1764 still take const bf16* row and bf16* row, and the design does not say they change to the typed views (source lens item 2). The load side is unchanged and right: "Wrap scratch without copying" covers full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2655 get_k_row<hw_kv>(slot, kv_head, off, dest). "copy paths" was kept although the intent lens asked to remove it (see the new defect). Severity of the finding was note, so the missing names are low risk, but the text does not yet carry what the corrected recommendation asked.

Still needed: Replace 'in model save paths, copy paths, and affected test callers' at :432 with 'in model.hpp store_k_block (the kout slice view at child model.hpp:2920; the conv[0] scratch at :2924), in the uniform-geometry forwarding overloads kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1752-1764 whose const bf16* and bf16* parameters become the typed views, and in the set_k_row and get_k_row callers of t/t_llama_unit.cpp, t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp and t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:101. copy_storage_slot calls neither routine.' Checker assessment: The STILL NEEDED list after round 3 had three items, all written for a design that kept a bf16_chunk override. The design instead adopted G12 option A (no override), which the round-3 lead allowed, and section 9 says so (:590). Under that choice: - Item 1 (exercise the override body by calling row.bf16_chunk(i) or assigning to a bf16 dmatensor) is void: there is no override body. The sentence it targeted is gone (design-r3.txt:440 versus design-r4.txt:467), and the design now states that the host-tensor consumer reads chunk() only (:253, :258, :467). Verified: tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:81-83 and :272-274 read rows through chunk(); only dmatensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:275-276 calls bf16_chunk. Acceptable. - Item 3 (optional objdump region for the bf16 row read) is void per the round-3 fairness-lens correction, which said it no longer serves detection. The design instead covers the moved bf16 load_row body (:523, lines kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2454 and :2462 verified) and warns that "A generic fp32 round trip can pass bit checks while adding work". Acceptable. - Item 2 (the cost clause: the fallback costs a shift, a NaN check, and a narrow per chunk, to be attached to the fallback sentence) is NOT met. The fallback sentence exists at :258 and states bit-exactness and the no-consumer reason, but no cost. The round-3 source-lens re-grader repeated this as an addition to the bf16_chunk row. Under option A the fallback is the shipped path for any bf16 expression read, so the clause records the trade-off the parent accepts. Verified cost from h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-110: without TRON_IGNORE_NAN two compares, a mask-and-not and a masked OR (the NaN check, :96-106), then _mm512_srli_epi32 (:108) and _mm512_cvtepi32_epi16 (:109); with the macro only the shift and the narrow (:93-94, :108-109). The clause's "NaN check" applies only to the macro-absent build, and all non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro (design :349), so the wording should say so. The round-1 parts (a) chunk-to-pair mechanics (:257, :262), (c) set/merge mechanics (:268, moved set_v bodies) and (d) the stride-2 rejection (:262) remain in the text; (b) the override signature is superseded by option A. Substance present, one concrete clause missing: partly. A lead who reads option A as voiding the whole residual could accept this as resolved; the missing clause is one sentence with low risk.

Still needed: Add one sentence to the bf16_chunk(i) row at design-r4.txt:258, after "Converting back preserves the stored bits under either NaN policy.": "The fallback costs a 16-bit shift and a narrow per chunk, plus a NaN check when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is absent [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-110]; the parent accepts this because no production path reads packed V through bf16_chunk()."

Resolved G09. Type constraints must be body static_asserts, not requires-clauses (round 3, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:298 "Type constraints are positive even rows and positive columns divisible by chunk_size. Put all owner, view, and row constraints in class-body static_assert statements, including the allowed element types. Do not add class-template requires clauses: the forward declarations are unconstrained and cannot include SIMD definitions. Keep stricter operation constraints, including the packed append width. The AMX kernels retain their fixed 64-token by 128-dimension shape. The child's packed-K owner and matrix view assert that fixed shape inside their definitions." design-r4.txt:428 "The child replaces kv_block::k with this selection. Put K shape and element constraints in class-body static_assert statements too. std::conditional_t must be able to name the unselected packed specialization for native geometries. A rejecting class-template constraint would fail before selection. ... Require 64-byte alignment, unchanged K/V offsets and block size, sizeof(k) == sizeof(v), and a 16,384-byte owner for 64 tokens by 128 dimensions." design-r4.txt:418 "Add unconstrained k_vnni_tensor, k_vnni_view, and k_vnni_row forward declarations to h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp, parallel to the V declarations." Section 9: design-r4.txt:558 "| G09 G10 G12 G13 G40 | Use class-body static_assert constraints. ..."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked the design to say, in section 5, that every owner/view/row constraint (even rows, columns divisible by chunk_size, T is bf16 or const bf16, the child's 64x128 owner shape) is a class-body static_assert and never a class-template requires-clause, with the two reasons (the intrinsics-free declarations header cannot name chunk_size or TRON_CHUNK_SIZE; std::conditional_t names k_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size> for every declared head size), and to repeat the two reasons under the k_storage snippet in section 7. :298 carries the rule, the element-type clause, the first reason and the fixed-shape placement; :428 carries the rule for K and the conditional_t reason; :418 states the child's K forward declarations are unconstrained. The word diff confirms these are round-4 insertions [design-wdiff.txt:256-260, :389]. Facts checked. (1) The declarations header cannot spell the columns constraint: h/tron/simd/auto.hpp@2880c3aa9b includes <immintrin.h> at :6, defines the TRON_CHUNK_SIZE macro at :17-21 and chunk_size at :86, so both spellings live in an intrinsics header. (2) The repository precedent that does not transfer: kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:538-540 forward-declares scaled_v_expr with requires(head_size % chunk_size == 0) and repeats it at :1988-1990; that header includes the intrinsics. (3) layout_on<head_size> is head_size == HEAD_SIZE_128 under TRON_K_VNNI and false otherwise [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:91-97], so the conditional_t at :426 names k_vnni_tensor<64, 64>, <64, 256> and <64, 512> as unselected branches. (4) Compile probes with g++ 11.4.0 -std=c++20 (files in the scratchpad agent-notes/b04/): b_requires.cpp puts the fixed shape in a requires-clause and fails at kv_block<64, 64> with "template constraint failure ... constraints not satisfied"; a_body_assert.cpp puts the same check in the class body behind an unconstrained forward declaration and compiles for kv_block<64, 64>, <64, 128>, <64, 256> and <64, 512>; a2.cpp (assert forced false) fails only through the selected kv_block<64, 128>. So :298's last sentence ("assert that fixed shape inside their definitions") and :428's conditional_t sentence are consistent, and the placement the design chose is one the round-3 source lens accepted ("a static_assert on the selected instance (or on the kernel boundary), never a constraint on k_vnni_tensor itself" in the C++ sense of a constraint). Wording note only: "the forward declarations are unconstrained and cannot include SIMD definitions" means the declarations header cannot include them; the meaning is clear from :243 and :299.

source re-grader (Resolved): Section 5 now says "Put all owner, view, and row constraints in class-body static_assert statements, including the allowed element types. Do not add class-template requires clauses: the forward declarations are unconstrained and cannot include SIMD definitions." and "The child's packed-K owner and matrix view assert that fixed shape inside their definitions." [design-r4.txt:298]. Section 7 repeats it under the k_storage snippet: "Put K shape and element constraints in class-body static_assert statements too. std::conditional_t must be able to name the unselected packed specialization for native geometries. A rejecting class-template constraint would fail before selection." and asks for sizeof(k) == sizeof(v) and a 16,384-byte owner [design-r4.txt:426-428]. The K forward declarations are unconstrained [design-r4.txt:418]. Facts checked: chunk_size is defined at h/tron/simd/auto.hpp@2880c3aa9b:86 and the TRON_CHUNK_SIZE macro at :17-21, in a header that includes <immintrin.h> at :6, so kv_cache_fwd.hpp cannot spell that constraint. The repository precedent of repeating a requires-clause on a forward declaration [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:538-540 and :1988-1990] works only because kv_cache.hpp includes the SIMD header. Probe with g++ 11.4.0 -std=c++20 (scratchpad/agent-notes/b04-g09/): an unconstrained forward declaration followed by a definition with requires(Cols % 16 == 0) fails with "redeclaration ... with different constraints"; k_vnni_tensor with requires(Cols == 128) fails at kv_block<64, 64> with "template constraint failure"; k_vnni_tensor with a class-body static_assert(Cols == 128 && Rows == 64) compiles for kv_block<64, 64>, kv_block<64, 128> and kv_block<64, 256> with the static_assert(sizeof(k) == sizeof(v)) in kv_block (return code 0). So every sentence of the fix is right. The child at 30c4ac82cb still has a raw array k [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2380] and no std::conditional_t; the design presents the snippet as the child's future change [design-r4.txt:428], which is consistent. Correction: To the round-3 design-text-lens correction, item (b) "do not make k_vnni_tensor a 64-by-128-only class, because the std::conditional_t names it for every declared head size": that is over-cautious. Naming a class template specialization as a std::conditional_t argument does not instantiate its body, so a class-body static_assert of the fixed shape never fires in the unselected branch (probe a_body_assert.cpp, g++ 11.4.0, return code 0). The design's choice at design-r4.txt:298 and :428 is valid. Minor wording note: the design gives the reason as "cannot include SIMD definitions" [design-r4.txt:298] and does not name tron/simd/auto.hpp or TRON_CHUNK_SIZE; the reason is right, only compressed.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The exact rule the recommendation asked for is in the body twice. Section 5 (design-r4.txt:298): "Put all owner, view, and row constraints in class-body static_assert statements, including the allowed element types. Do not add class-template requires clauses: the forward declarations are unconstrained and cannot include SIMD definitions." Section 7 under the k_storage snippet (design-r4.txt:428): "Put K shape and element constraints in class-body static_assert statements too. std::conditional_t must be able to name the unselected packed specialization for native geometries. A rejecting class-template constraint would fail before selection." Both C++ claims are right. A requires-clause on k_vnni_tensor fails when kv_block<64,64> is instantiated: g++ 11.4.0 -std=c++20 reports "template constraint failure for template<...> requires Rows == 64 && Cols == 128 class tron::k_vnni_tensor" (probe $S/agent-notes/b04/g09_requires.cpp). The design's chosen alternative, "The child's packed-K owner and matrix view assert that fixed shape inside their definitions" (design-r4.txt:298), compiles for kv_block<64,64>, kv_block<64,256> and kv_block<64,128> with sizeof(k_vnni_tensor<64,128>) == 16384: std::conditional_t names the type as a template argument without instantiating it, so a class-body static_assert never runs for the unselected branch (probe $S/agent-notes/b04/g09_body_assert.cpp, "COMPILES"). The forward declarations at design-r4.txt:243 and :418 are unconstrained as the rule requires. The intrinsics fact behind the rule holds: chunk_size and the TRON_CHUNK_SIZE macro live only in h/tron/simd/auto.hpp, which includes <immintrin.h> [auto.hpp@2880c3aa9b:6, :18, :20, :86]. Section 9 at design-r4.txt:558 matches the body. Note, no status change: the design compresses the reason to "cannot include SIMD definitions" and does not name chunk_size, TRON_CHUNK_SIZE or tron/simd/auto.hpp as the recommendation's explanatory sentences did; the rule an implementer must follow is exact, so the missing explanation is a note. Correction: One correction to the round-3 verifier guidance, not to the design: the design-text lens said "do not make k_vnni_tensor a 64-by-128-only class, because the std::conditional_t names it for every declared head size", and the source lens said the 64x128 check must be "never a constraint on k_vnni_tensor itself". That hazard applies only to a requires-clause (a constraint in the C++ sense). A class-body static_assert inside k_vnni_tensor, which the design chose at design-r4.txt:298, is checked only on instantiation, and std::conditional_t does not instantiate the unselected type. The probe $S/agent-notes/b04/g09_body_assert.cpp compiles with g++ 11.4.0 -std=c++20. So the design's choice is a valid alternative to placing the check in kv_block, and it matches the reviewer's sketch, which uses class-body static_asserts.

Resolved G10. Five view members required 'by expression consumers' that no consumer reads; valid() implies a null view the design does not provide (round 3, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:253 "The matrix supplies operator[] returning its row expression. The named host-tensor constructor reads row chunk() values. Add no dim, element, const_element, shape0(), or valid() member without a caller. No null-view state or default view constructor is proposed. Leave the rank-1 expression concept unchanged. The named V expression consumer is the ordinary host-tensor construction check in section 8. Production V paths continue to use bulk operations. Native K remains compatible with dotter, the existing query/key dot-product helper. [S2][S3][S4]" design-r4.txt:467 "| Expression reads: existing tensor/cache cases | Construct a host tensor from the packed matrix view and compare its logical values with independent patterns. This exercises row chunk() . ..." Section 9: design-r4.txt:558 "Keep only expression members with named consumers."

Checker assessment: The recommendation asked to replace "Supply dim, element, const_element, shape0(), and valid() as required by expression consumers" with: the matrix provides operator[]; the named consumer (the host tensor built from expr<B, R, D>) needs only operator[] from the matrix and chunk()/bf16_chunk() from the row; add the five members only when a named caller reads them; valid() would need a null view the design does not provide. :253 now says exactly this, including the null-state sentence, and :467 names the consumer and what it exercises. The word diff confirms the replacement [design-wdiff.txt:156-161]. The design chose the first option (drop the members) rather than the alternative (keep them for parity and define the null state); either option resolves the item. Facts checked. (1) The rank-2 host-tensor constructor tensor(expr<B, d0, d1, ds...> const& rhs) does std::construct_at(&data[i], rhs[i]) for each row [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:270-275], so it reads only operator[]. (2) The rank-1 constructor tensor(expr<B, N> const& rhs) calls rhs.chunk(i) for i < N / chunk_size and rhs.last() only when N % chunk_size != 0 [tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:79-85]; the supported head sizes 64, 128, 256 and 512 (design-r4.txt:224, :229-232) are multiples of 16, so "reads row chunk() values" is right and last() is not needed. (3) The expr base classes reference none of dim, element, const_element, shape0 or valid: the rank-n base has self() and operator[] [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:45-66]; the rank-1 base has chunk, bf16_chunk, fp16_chunk, last and size [expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:86-135]. (4) valid() on the existing view means data != nullptr and depends on the defaulted nullptr constructor [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:43, :57-59], so "No null-view state or default view constructor is proposed" is the right way to drop valid(). (5) The only test readers of ::dim and valid() are on the native K view returned by page->k [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:704-709], which the parent keeps as the ordinary view (design-r4.txt:280), so they are not packed-view consumers.

source re-grader (Resolved): The sentence now reads "The matrix supplies operator[] returning its row expression. The named host-tensor constructor reads row chunk() values. Add no dim, element, const_element, shape0(), or valid() member without a caller. No null-view state or default view constructor is proposed." [design-r4.txt:253]. That covers the corrected recommendation, including the null-state decision the intent lens asked for (the design chose "no default constructor and no valid()"). The test row names the consumer: "Construct a host tensor from the packed matrix view ... This exercises row chunk() ." [design-r4.txt:467]. Facts checked: the rank-2 host tensor constructor loops std::construct_at(&data[i], rhs[i]) [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:270-275]; the rank-1 constructor loops store_chunk(i, rhs.chunk(i)) and reads last() only when N % chunk_size != 0 [:79-84]; head sizes 64, 128, 256 and 512 are multiples of 16, so last() is not needed. The rank-N expr base uses only self()[i] [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:45-66] and the rank-1 base only chunk() and the bf16_chunk fallback [:86-116], so no dim, element, const_element, shape0() or valid() is demanded by the base. The ordinary view's null state comes from its default nullptr constructor and valid() [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:43, :57-59]; the design declines both for packed views. The words "Default construction" at design-r4.txt:249 and :363 refer to the owner and the block, not the view, so there is no contradiction. The checker's quotes exist at :253, :467 and :558.

Resolved G12. bf16_chunk override and decltype test protect a test-only path; the decltype check belongs in the header, not the suite (round 3, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:258 "| bf16_chunk(i) | Use the inherited expression fallback. Logical fp32 reads place the stored bf16 bits in the upper half and leave the lower half zero. Converting back preserves the stored bits under either NaN policy. The parent adds no direct-bit override or member-pointer assertion. Its named host-tensor consumer reads chunk() , not bf16_chunk() . This adopts the smaller round-3 G12 option in place of the earlier override proposal. [S15] [G12] |" design-r4.txt:253 "The named host-tensor constructor reads row chunk() values." design-r4.txt:345 "| Expression reads | bf16_chunk() preserves stored bits. Existing destination types retain their own conversion rules. |" design-r4.txt:389 (step 1) "Keep the inherited bf16_chunk fallback and no custom override." design-r4.txt:467 "| Expression reads: existing tensor/cache cases | Construct a host tensor from the packed matrix view and compare its logical values with independent patterns. This exercises row chunk() . Exact bf16 bulk-load and token-copy checks belong to the conversion cases. No custom bf16_chunk override or signature test is proposed. | Broken logical row indexing, extraction, or host-tensor expression compatibility. |" Section 9: design-r4.txt:558 "Omit the bf16_chunk override and its signature test. Use the inherited fallback."; :607 and :632 "The round-3 G12 choice supersedes the custom bf16_chunk override and its structural test. Use the inherited bit-exact fallback."

Checker assessment: The design picks round-3 option A and states the reason: the only named consumer reads chunk(), so an override would speed up nothing the parent exercises (:258). Option A asked for three things and all are present: the row says v_vnni_row does not override bf16_chunk and the fallback is bit-exact because the low 16 bits are zero (:258); the only consumer is the section-8 host-tensor check (:253, :258, :467); the decltype sentence and "Bit patterns alone cannot detect the bit-exact fallback" are deleted from the section-8 row (design-r3.txt:440 versus design-r4.txt:467; grep decltype over design-r4.txt finds nothing). The source-lens corrections for option A are also met: :345 keeps "bf16_chunk() preserves stored bits", which stays true under the fallback, and the section-9 rows :558, :607, :632 say the override was superseded, not corrected. The round-3 lead said either option closes the finding. Facts checked: - Detection: h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:110-117 if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk) return self().bf16_chunk(i); else return fp32s_to_bf16s(self().chunk(i));. With no override in the row the fallback branch is taken. RIGHT. - Low half zero: the extraction the row copies (get_v(float*), kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2420 _mm512_slli_epi32(both, 16); :2429 _mm512_and_si512(both, hi_16_of_32) with 0xffff0000) leaves the low 16 bits of every lane zero. RIGHT. - Bit-exact under either NaN policy: h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-110. Without TRON_IGNORE_NAN the function ORs 0x00010000 only where the exponent field equals 0x7f800000 AND the low 16 bits are nonzero (:99-106); with a zero low half that mask is clear; then _mm512_srli_epi32(y, 16) and _mm512_cvtepi32_epi16 return the original bf16 bits (:108-109). With the macro the shift and narrow run alone. RIGHT. - Consumer: the rank-2 host tensor constructor does std::construct_at(&data[i], rhs[i]) per row (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:272-274) and the rank-1 constructor calls rhs.chunk(i) (:81-83); only dmatensor<bf16> calls rhs.bf16_chunk(i) (h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:275-276), and the design no longer names that fixture. "reads chunk(), not bf16_chunk()" RIGHT. - The [G12] link at :258 points at the live review page anchor (design-r4-links.tsv), which the round-4 page must keep.

New defect raised by the checker (note): Claim: the source list keeps a link labelled as if an override existed. Design quote: design-r4.txt:669 "| S15 | ... [bf16 override detection] ..."; the link target is h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp#L110-L117 at 2880c3aa9b (design-r4-links.tsv:443). Source evidence: those lines are the expr base's member-pointer comparison that selects either an override or the fp32s_to_bf16s fallback (expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:110-117). The design now relies on the fallback branch of that same code (:258), so the label describes the source accurately but could make a reader think an override is still proposed. Recommendation (optional): relabel to "bf16_chunk override check and fallback". No body change is needed.

source re-grader (Resolved): The design picks option A and states the reason: "Use the inherited expression fallback ... The parent adds no direct-bit override or member-pointer assertion. Its named host-tensor consumer reads chunk(), not bf16_chunk(). This adopts the smaller round-3 G12 option in place of the earlier override proposal" [design-r4.txt:258]. The decltype sentence and the hardware-tensor fixture sentence from round 3 (design-r3.txt:440) are gone: grep of design-r4.txt for "decltype" and "hardware-tensor fixture" returns nothing. The Expression-reads row now says "This exercises row chunk() ... No custom bf16_chunk override or signature test is proposed" [design-r4.txt:467]. Step 1 repeats the choice [design-r4.txt:389]. Section 6 keeps "bf16_chunk() preserves stored bits" [design-r4.txt:345], which stays true under the fallback, as the source-lens correction noted. Section 9 says the override was superseded, not corrected [design-r4.txt:558, :607, :632]. Every source fact is right. expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:110-117 selects fp32s_to_bf16s(self().chunk(i)) when the derived class declares no bf16_chunk. fp32s_to_bf16s (h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-110) ORs 0x00010000 only where the exponent field is saturated AND the low 16 bits are nonzero (:99-106), then shifts right by 16 and narrows (:108-109); with TRON_IGNORE_NAN it only shifts and narrows (:93-94). A chunk() value from the shift-left-16 or the 0xffff0000 mask has zero low 16 bits, so the stored bits return unchanged under both policies: "Converting back preserves the stored bits under either NaN policy" is right. "Its named host-tensor consumer reads chunk()" is right: the rank-2 tensor constructor runs std::construct_at(&data[i], rhs[i]) (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:272-274) and the rank-1 constructor runs store_chunk(i, rhs.chunk(i)) (:81-84). The only bf16_chunk callers at that commit are dmatensor.hpp:276, :296, :316, :329 and the slice expression at expr.hpp:716 (git grep over h src t); none is in the parent's plan. The intent-lens verifier preferred option B, but the round-3 lead's final note said either option closes the finding, and the design states its reason, so the lead's rule for two-option items applies.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The design picks option A and says so. The bf16_chunk row now reads: "Use the inherited expression fallback. Logical fp32 reads place the stored bf16 bits in the upper half and leave the lower half zero. Converting back preserves the stored bits under either NaN policy. The parent adds no direct-bit override or member-pointer assertion. Its named host-tensor consumer reads chunk(), not bf16_chunk(). This adopts the smaller round-3 G12 option in place of the earlier override proposal." [design-r4.txt:258]. The decltype sentence of the round-3 Expression reads row [design-r3.txt:440] is gone; the row now says "This exercises row chunk(). ... No custom bf16_chunk override or signature test is proposed." [design-r4.txt:467]. Step 1 says "Keep the inherited bf16_chunk fallback and no custom override." [design-r4.txt:389]. Section 6 keeps "bf16_chunk() preserves stored bits" [design-r4.txt:345], which stays true under the fallback, as the source lens noted. The section-9 rows say the override is omitted or superseded rather than corrected [design-r4.txt:558, :607, :632]. The facts are right. The expression base falls back to fp32s_to_bf16s(self().chunk(i)) when no override exists [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:110-116]. With TRON_IGNORE_NAN, fp32s_to_bf16s shifts right by 16 bits and narrows, so the upper half is returned unchanged; without the macro it sets bit 0x00010000 only when the exponent field is saturated AND the low 16 bits are nonzero, so a zero low half is returned unchanged [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-109]. Both extraction halves leave the low 16 bits zero (shift left by 16, or mask with 0xffff0000) [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2422, :2429]. So "under either NaN policy" is right. The rank-1 host tensor constructor reads rhs.chunk(i), never bf16_chunk [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:80-84], so the consumer sentence is right. Correction: No correction to the checker. The intent-lens correction preferred option B and asked that option A be labeled as a departure with a reason. The design labels it ("adopts the smaller round-3 G12 option in place of the earlier override proposal") and gives the reason (bit-exact fallback under either policy; the named consumer reads chunk()) [design-r4.txt:258]. Under the lead's rule, either option with a stated reason resolves the item.

Resolved G13. even_part and odd_part are private members of scaled_v_expr; the row's chunk() cannot reuse them as written (round 3, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:262 "A 16-lane pair chunk contains 32 bf16 values in 64 bytes. Copy the extraction pattern from the existing float get_v loop into v_vnni_row::chunk(): shift left by 16 bits for even tokens and mask with 0xffff0000 for odd tokens. The similarly named even_part and odd_part helpers are private to scaled_v_expr and cannot be called by the row. Keep the direct narrowing in the moved bf16 load_row loop. A stride-2 ordinary view has the right addresses but uses scalar extraction. [S5]" design-r4.txt:269 "load_row moves today's get_v loops. Wrap existing caller-owned scratch in the ordinary contiguous destination view." design-r4.txt:523 "Also locate V row unpack, page::get_v → load_row, at saved-main t_llama_unit.cpp:819,1575,2038. Its bf16 path uses one _mm512_cvtepi32_epi16 narrowing per 16 dimensions at kv_cache.hpp:2454,2462." Section 9, design-r4.txt:558 "Copy the row-extraction pattern into the V implementation."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked for three things: point chunk() at the non-private get_v(float*) extraction instead of the private helpers, say that even_part and odd_part stay private in kv_cache.hpp and cannot be called from the row, and say how bf16_chunk reuses the get_v(bf16*) narrowing. The body now does the first two exactly (:262), and the third is void because the design adopted G12 option A: v_vnni_row has no bf16_chunk body (:258, :389). The narrowing template is kept where it will live, in the moved bf16 load_row loop (:262, :269), and the objdump list cites its two lines (:523). The word "pattern" and the verb "Copy" are back, which is what the lead's note said the round-3 text had lost. Facts checked against the source (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b): - get_v(float*) even-token extraction is _mm512_slli_epi32(both, 16) at :2420; odd-token extraction is _mm512_and_si512(both, hi_16_of_32) with hi_16_of_32 = _mm512_set1_epi32(0xffff0000) at :2424-2429. "shift left by 16 bits for even tokens and mask with 0xffff0000 for odd tokens" RIGHT. - private: at :1996 inside detail::scaled_v_expr; odd_part at :2000-2002 reads the member hi_16_of_32 (:1997); even_part at :2005-2007. "private to scaled_v_expr and cannot be called by the row" RIGHT. - get_v(bf16*) narrows with _mm512_cvtepi32_epi16(both) at :2454 (even) and _mm512_cvtepi32_epi16(_mm512_srli_epi32(both, 16)) at :2462 (odd). "direct narrowing in the moved bf16 load_row loop" and the cited lines 2454,2462 RIGHT. - The recommendation's include-direction clause ("kv_cache.hpp includes v_vnni.hpp, not the reverse") is not spelled out for V; the design gives the stronger reason (private members) and states that v_vnni.hpp supplies the definitions the cache uses (:300, :389-390). The corrected recommendation does not require both reasons, so this is not a residual. - The design cites no line range for the float get_v loop (the recommendation gave kv_cache.hpp:2416-2431). The lead's note asked for the pointer to get_v(float*), which the text gives by name. Not required.

source re-grader (Resolved): The extraction paragraph now points at the non-private get_v loop instead of the private helpers: "Copy the extraction pattern from the existing float get_v loop into v_vnni_row::chunk(): shift left by 16 bits for even tokens and mask with 0xffff0000 for odd tokens" and "even_part and odd_part helpers are private to scaled_v_expr and cannot be called by the row" [design-r4.txt:262]. Source facts are right. page::get_v(float*) at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2408-2433 uses _mm512_slli_epi32(both, 16) for an even token (:2420) and _mm512_and_si512(both, hi_16_of_32) with hi_16_of_32 = _mm512_set1_epi32(0xffff0000) for an odd token (:2424, :2429). even_part and odd_part are under private: at :1996-2007 and have no caller at that commit (git grep). The row address contract, pair_base = plane + (token / 2) * 2 * D and chunk i at pair_base + 2 * chunk_size * i [design-r4.txt:257], matches get_v's base v[i_page / 2] (:2414) and its load at v_ptr + i * 2 with i stepping by 16 (:2416-2418), given bf16s v[page_size / 2][head_size / chunk_size * 2] (:2198): one pair row holds 2 * D bf16 values and one chunk is 32 bf16 values = 64 bytes. The bf16 half of the recommendation is met in the form the G12 option-A choice allows: there is no bf16_chunk override, and the design keeps the direct _mm512_cvtepi32_epi16 narrowing in the moved bf16 load_row loop [design-r4.txt:262, :272], citing lines 2454 and 2462 [design-r4.txt:523]; verified at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2454 (even) and :2462 (odd, after _mm512_srli_epi32(both, 16)). The recommendation's include-direction sentence (kv_cache.hpp includes v_vnni.hpp, not the reverse) is not stated verbatim, but the reason the design gives (private members of another class) is true and sufficient on its own. Correction: Two citation notes, no status change. (1) Design, note level: the [S5] tag at design-r4.txt:262 resolves to kv_cache.hpp@f46e48ba L2055-L2065 (the padding Note) and L2289-L2398 (the set_v bodies) [design-r4-links.tsv:407-408]. The design's own S21 link "[Float extraction and bf16 narrowing]" (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b#L2416-L2463) [design-r4-links.tsv:492] is the right citation for that paragraph. (2) Checker: the load_row sentence quoted as design-r4.txt:269 is at design-r4.txt:272. Line 268 is the parameter-families code block and line 269 is blank.

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked for one child bullet: the three K forward declarations in h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp, and the resulting by-value qk_vnni_128x4 declaration in the intrinsics-free interface header. The body now carries both, as a new bullet in the child adaptation list [design-r4.txt:418]. The word diff confirms the bullet is new in this revision [design-wdiff.txt:385]. Checked facts. (1) The reason the tensor header cannot be included: h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:8 includes tron/simd/auto.hpp, and h/tron/simd/auto.hpp@2880c3aa9b:6 includes <immintrin.h>. The K view and row inherit expr [design-r4.txt:416, :434], so their defining header carries intrinsics. The design's rule at :299 and :418 is consistent with that. (2) The declaration's other arguments match the child's current signature: h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@30c4ac82cb:251-254 declares qk_vnni_128x4(const bf16* k_vnni_plane, const bf16* q_rows, float* s, size_t s_stride_floats) noexcept. Only the K argument changes, as the design says. (3) The forward declarations are 'unconstrained' and 'parallel to the V declarations': the V declarations at design-r4.txt:243-245 use template <size_t Rows, size_t Cols> class v_vnni_tensor; and so on, and :298 forbids class-template requires clauses. Consistent. (4) The include instruction targets the right files: src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@30c4ac82cb:14 already includes tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp (which the design makes include the tensor header, :417), and t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@30c4ac82cb:196 defines the fake qk_vnni_128x4 outside the #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH block that starts at :207, so it needs the complete view type. (5) The source-lens correction proposed a literal clause 'amx_attn_iface.hpp includes only kv_cache_fwd.hpp'. The design did not add it. That is right: the header also includes <cstddef>, <type_traits> and common/numerics/bf16.hpp [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@30c4ac82cb:109-112], so 'only' would be false. The design's 'remains free of intrinsics' [:299] plus 'without intrinsics' [:418] and step 4's 'Keep the interface header free of intrinsics' [:391] state the real constraint. (6) The design-text lens asked to drop the include sentence as redundant with :299. The design kept a specific version of it [:418]. Redundant but harmless. The lead's final edit list item 7 [r3-findings.md:28] asked for exactly the forward declarations in kv_cache_fwd.hpp so the interface header can declare qk_vnni_128x4 by value. Done.

Resolved G19. for_each_active_slot visits logical slots, not physical; 'logical alias' is undefined and cannot occur in a fixed layout (round 3, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:367 "For heterogeneous geometry, enumerate physical storage offsets once and select only slots in the just-allocated arena. Restoring the reclaimable arena must not restart objects in the retained arena. Reuse book::for_each_active_slot, which calls the lambda once per active logical slot with its compile-time geometry. Compute its physical offset with kv_storage_offset(slot), as fill_random does. Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:394 "| 6. A local or properly aligned heap owner is suitable." design-r4.txt:400 "- Use the existing test conversion bf16_rne (round a float to bf16 using nearest-even rounding) to construct 64-byte-aligned source rows from the logical input. Append all 64 tokens in order with append_v_row through its bf16 input path. Pass owner.as_view() to the kernel's read-only parameter." design-r4.txt:401 "- Keep the test's independent pair-interleave formula as expected physical bytes. Copy bytes out of the trivially copyable owner into a plain test buffer and compare them. Do not copy hand-packed input bytes into the owner in these fixtures. This fixture rule verifies the public typed write path. It is not a claim that byte copying into a trivially copyable owner is illegal C++." design-r4.txt:402 "- Compute the numerical reference from the original logical input with the same existing bf16_rne conversion. Do not derive expected values from the typed view under test." design-r4.txt:403 "- The QK case retains qk_inputs::k. At its kernel call, wrap that aligned fixture array explicitly in const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64,HEAD_SIZE_128>. The fake QK definition changes its parameter type only. Production calls use the page's whole-plane accessor. [S21]" Section 9, design-r4.txt:565 "| G22 | Give the PV numerics fixture an aligned typed V owner. Fill it through typed operations, pass its read-only view, and compare bytes copied out against the independent packing formula. State the fixture policy for hand-packed input bytes. [Numerics fixture] [Parent test migration] | Run the real numerics case. A signature-only fake cannot prove the packed fixture is correct. |"

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation (design-text and intent lenses) asked the design to say that the PV case's std::vector page moves into a v_vnni_tensor<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> owner (16,384 bytes, 64-byte aligned), which public fill route to use, that owner.as_view() is the kernel argument, that the pair-formula check runs on bytes copied out of the owner, whether a memcpy of hand-packed bytes into the owner is allowed, and that the QK case keeps an explicit const_native_k_view wrap. The body text at design-r4.txt:399-403 states every one of these. Step 6 (design-r4.txt:394) points to that section, so the fix is in the body and not only in section 9. The section-9 row (design-r4.txt:565) matches the body. Facts checked in the fix: - The hand-packed page exists as described. t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:199 declares the logical input std::vector<float> v(PAGE_TOKENS_64 * HEAD_SIZE_128). Line 203 declares std::vector<tron::bf16> v_page(...). Lines 204-211 fill it with the pair formula through tron::bf16::from_bits(bf16_rne(...)). Lines 226-227 pass v_page.data() to weights_times_v_128x4. Lines 238-239 read v_page back by the same formula for the reference. So the design's "hand-packed std::vector<bf16> kernel input" and "independent pair-interleave formula" are right. - bf16_rne is an existing test helper. t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:42-47 defines uint16_t bf16_rne(float f) with round-to-nearest-even. The design's definition "round a float to bf16 using nearest-even rounding" is right. - The owner size is right. 64 tokens x 128 dimensions x 2 bytes per bf16 = 16,384 bytes. - The fill route exists in the design's own interface. append_v_row takes const_view<Source, true, Dma, seq<D>, sseq<1>> src with Source = bf16, fp16 or float (design-r4.txt:268, :270). The bf16 path preserves exact bits (design-r4.txt:343). Appending tokens 0..63 in order works with the even-zeroes-partner / odd-merges rule (design-r4.txt:271). - The reference route is equivalent to today's. Today's reference at :238-239 reads the hand-packed bf16 values, which were produced by bf16_rne from v. Reading bf16_rne(v[t * HEAD_SIZE_128 + d]) directly gives the same values, so design-r4.txt:402 changes no expected number. - The QK case's array is aligned. t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:65-68 struct alignas(64) qk_inputs { tron::bf16 k[PAGE_TOKENS_64 * HEAD_SIZE_128]; ... }, called at :158-159 with in->k. The explicit const_view pointer constructor exists (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:296). - The fakes need only the signature change. t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:180-181 and :185 define the fakes with const bf16* first parameters and never read them. The design's "The fake QK definition changes its parameter type only" is right; the PV fake is covered by design-r4.txt:288 "Type only the cache-plane arguments below." - The memcpy policy is stated the way the lead asked. The lead note said "the design should state whether tests may do it rather than the finding forbidding it". design-r4.txt:401 forbids it in these fixtures and says why, and says this is not a legality claim. That is the intent-lens option ("Prefer the append_v_row route").

New defect raised by the checker (note): Claim: the fixture route at design-r4.txt:400 depends on an implicit writable-to-read-only view conversion that the design never declares implicit. Design quote: "Pass owner.as_view() to the kernel's read-only parameter." (design-r4.txt:400). The owner is a non-const lvalue, so as_view() & returns v_vnni_view<bf16, 64, 128> (design-r4.txt:250). The kernel parameter is v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> (design-r4.txt:290). The contract says only "Allow writable-to-read-only conversion only" (design-r4.txt:259) and "Accept writable-to-read-only matrix conversion only" (design-r4.txt:465); neither says the converting constructor is implicit. If an implementer makes it explicit, the sentence at :400 does not compile as written, and the production PV call would also need an explicit cast. Source evidence: the existing precedent is implicit, const_view(view const& other) noexcept at h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:299, in contrast to the explicit pointer constructor at :296. Recommendation: at design-r4.txt:259 write "Allow an implicit writable-to-read-only conversion only, like the existing const_view(view const&) converting constructor", and in the section-8 row at :465 make the positive check std::is_convertible_v<v_vnni_view<bf16,R,D>, v_vnni_view<const bf16,R,D>>.

source re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation asked the design to name the typed route for the PV fixture of t/t_amx_numerics.cpp, to state the memcpy policy, and to keep the QK fixture's explicit K wrap. The design now has a dedicated subsection [design-r4.txt:397-403], linked from step 6 [design-r4.txt:394] and from the section-9 row [design-r4.txt:565]. Every checkable fact in it is right. (1) The PV case builds a std::vector<tron::bf16> page by hand and passes v_page.data() to the kernel [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203-211, :226-227]; the design replaces it with a v_vnni_tensor<PAGE_TOKENS_64,HEAD_SIZE_128> owner of 16,384 bytes (64 tokens x 128 dimensions x 2 bytes) with 64-byte alignment [design-r4.txt:399]. (2) bf16_rne exists in the test as a float-to-bf16 round-to-nearest-even helper [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:42-47]; the design uses it to build aligned source rows and appends all 64 tokens in order through append_v_row's bf16 path [design-r4.txt:400]. The bf16 append path preserves exact input bits by the design's own conversion table [design-r4.txt:342], so the stored bits equal today's hand-packed bits. Appending in token order matters because an even append zeros its odd partner [design-r4.txt:268]; the design says 'in order'. (3) owner.as_view() is passed to the read-only kernel parameter [design-r4.txt:400]; the owner has as_view() & and the writable-to-read-only conversion is the one allowed conversion [design-r4.txt:248, :259], and the kernel parameter is v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> [design-r4.txt:290]. (4) The pair-interleave formula survives only as an expected-bytes check on bytes copied OUT of the trivially copyable owner [design-r4.txt:401, owner triviality at :247], which is what the lead note and the intent-lens correction asked. (5) The memcpy policy is stated: no copying of hand-packed bytes into the owner in these fixtures, with the explicit statement that this is a fixture rule and not a C++ legality claim [design-r4.txt:401]; this matches the lead note ('the design should state whether tests may do it'). (6) The numerical reference is computed from the logical float input through bf16_rne [design-r4.txt:402]; today the reference reads v_page by the layout formula [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:238-239], and v_page was itself built with bf16_rne from the same floats [:207-208], so the values are identical and the layout formula leaves the reference, as the source-lens verifier suggested. (8) The fake QK definition changes only its parameter type [design-r4.txt:403]; the fakes sit outside any #ifdef [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:166-190]. The section-9 row [design-r4.txt:565] matches the body, and its links [Numerics fixture] -> #fixtures and [Parent test migration] -> #files resolve (both ids exist in the HTML). The new section 'AMX numerics fixture migration' carries every part. It replaces the hand-packed std::vector<bf16> page with a v_vnni_tensor<PAGE_TOKENS_64,HEAD_SIZE_128> owner of 16,384 bytes at 64-byte alignment, local or aligned heap [design-r4.txt:399]. It names the fill route: bf16_rne rows, 64 append_v_row calls in order through the bf16 input path, then owner.as_view() to the kernel's read-only parameter [design-r4.txt:400]. It keeps the pair-interleave formula as expected physical bytes compared against bytes copied out of the owner, and it states the fixture policy: do not copy hand-packed input bytes into the owner, while saying that such a copy is not illegal C++ [design-r4.txt:401]. It computes the numerical reference from the logical input through bf16_rne, not from the view under test [design-r4.txt:402], which is the source-lens optional addition. The QK case keeps qk_inputs::k behind an explicit const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64,HEAD_SIZE_128> wrap and the fake changes only its parameter type [design-r4.txt:403]. Step 6 points at this section [design-r4.txt:394] and the section-9 row matches the body [design-r4.txt:565]. Checkable facts are right: the PV case builds v_page by hand at t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:197-211 and passes v_page.data() at :225-226; the reference reads v_page by the formula at :238-239; bf16_rne is defined at :42 and returns uint16_t; qk_inputs is alignas(64) at :65-68; 64 x 128 x 2 bytes = 16,384 bytes. Correction: Note, no change required: bf16_rne returns uint16_t, so the aligned source rows need tron::bf16::from_bits as the existing fill does [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:42-45, :208-209]. Note: 'Pass owner.as_view()' [design-r4.txt:400] from a non-const owner relies on the writable-to-read-only view conversion being implicit. The design allows that conversion [design-r4.txt:259] and treats it as not applying under template deduction [design-r4.txt:432], which fits an implicit converting constructor like the existing const_view(view const&) [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:299]. If an implementer marks it explicit, the test needs std::as_const(owner).as_view() instead. Low risk.

Checker assessment: The design adds a new subsection (design-r4.txt:500-504) that carries every element of the corrected recommendation (the lead's intent-lens version): the log path form, what the job log shows and does not show, where the Catch2 case lines live, that successful runs upload nothing, how to identify the runner (Set up job), where to read the two store paths (the Restore exact Nix test runtime print), the deletion mechanism (next checkout) plus Slice's 10-run cap, immediate preservation, the unreachable-runner fallback with a labeled local run, and the statement that upload-on-success is a separate CI change. RIGHT. - Case lines only in files: bin/slice:3148 log_path = run_dir / f"{name}.log"; :3174 open(log_path, "w"); :3182-3187 Popen(stdout=log_f, stderr=STDOUT). RIGHT. - Upload only on failure: gcp-nix.yml:580-587 "Upload Slice test logs", if: failure() && env.RUN_TESTS == 'true', path ${{ github.workspace }}/logs-*/run-*. RIGHT. - Store paths: gcp-nix.yml:545 step name "Restore exact Nix test runtime"; bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py:133-136 prints "Preparing test runtime: {canonical_build}; environment={canonical_environment}". RIGHT. - Next checkout cleans: the Test host and Test FPGA jobs check out with actions/checkout@de0fac2e and only fetch-depth: 0 [gcp-nix.yml:539-541, :606-608]; action.yml at de0fac2e lines 57-59 (read via gh api) defines clean with default true = "git clean -ffdx && git reset --hard HEAD"; .gitignore:68 lists logs-*/, and -x removes ignored paths. RIGHT. - 10 run directories: bin/slice:114 RETENTION = 10; :2766-2768 prunes while len(existing) >= RETENTION. RIGHT. - Runner pool: gcp-nix.yml:534 runs-on [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512]. "Set up job" is GitHub's own first step of every job (facts-r4). - Rendering: the HTML escapes the placeholders (&lt;checkout&gt;, &lt;hostname&gt;, &lt;path&gt;; grep on the HTML finds 1 escaped and 0 raw <checkout>), so a browser shows them. The word diff's "Logs: /logs-/run-NNNN" (design-wdiff.txt:434) is an extraction artifact, not a page defect. - "Do not access another Delphi or Andoria host" restates the user's machine rule (only delphi-3bda unless directed). Every checkable fact in the fix is right, and the text now specifies what the corrected recommendation asked.

New defect raised by the checker (note): Claim: the design presents runner access as the normal path and the fallback as the exception, but under its own host rule the fallback will be the usual case. Design quote: design-r4.txt:503 "Preserve logs immediately if the runner is accessible within the permitted host scope." and :504 "Do not access another Delphi or Andoria host to retrieve logs." with :512 "Use only delphi-3bda for real hardware tests." Source evidence: the Test host job runs on any runner labeled [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512] [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:534]; the round-3 evidence observed two executed Test host jobs on andoria-09 and delphi-3af6 (facts-r4: a real 2026-09-19 job log printed "Logs: /opt/positron/runners/delphi-3af6-0/_work/tron/tron/logs-delphi-3af6/run-0000"). Those hosts are outside the permitted scope, so the per-case CI logs are unreachable by rule whenever the job does not land on delphi-3bda. Whether delphi-3bda is in the runner pool and how often a job lands there is Insufficient data from the repository. Consequence: :504 "Resolve that evidence gap before committing new tests under the repository rule, or obtain its explicit user exception" will apply on most runs, so the implementer should plan for the user-exception path from the start. Recommendation: add one sentence to :503: "The runner is chosen from the labeled pool and is usually not delphi-3bda, so expect the fallback below to be the normal case and ask for the user exception early."

Facts checked in the fix: - The constants and the case exist at the cited lines. t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:84-123 hold the requires-expression constants (page_k_accepts_raw_index at :84-86 through page_scaled_v_accepts_geometry at :118-123). Line 316 is TEST_CASE("attention operations resolve to typed KV slots", "[kv_data]") and its STATIC_REQUIRE / STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE block runs :320-342. - The kernel declarations are visible in t_llama_unit without a new include. t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:66 includes tron/models/model.hpp. h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:53 includes tron/models/self_attention.hpp. h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:21 includes tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp, before the only conditional in that region (#if at :30). git grep -n '^#(if|endif|else)' over h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@2880c3aa9b returns nothing, so the declarations at :219-222 and :230-233 inside namespace tron::amx_attn_h128g4 (:114) are unconditional. This confirms the G30 source-lens chain and shows the M03 re-grader's "t_llama_unit adds that include" is not needed. The design's required positive checks also prevent a STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE from passing because a name is undeclared. - The four rejections are implementable as stated. const_view's pointer constructor is explicit at both ranks (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:296 and :373), so a bf16* or const bf16* argument to the const_native_k_view parameter fails overload resolution without a view.hpp change. The design gives v_vnni_view no public raw-pointer constructor (design-r4.txt:259), so weights_times_v_128x4 rejects raw pointers, and no conversion from const_view to v_vnni_view exists, so it rejects const_native_k_view. The kernel parameters are those at design-r4.txt:290. - The checks compile in both widths. Typed kernel declarations and packed class definitions stay available at both chunk widths (design-r4.txt:296), so t_llama_unit compiles the constants under 8 lanes too. Not done, cosmetic: the source-lens correction also asked to "mention the same two sites in the section-9 M03 row". design-r4.txt:620 still says only "inside an existing suite". The body (:465) and the G30 row (:570) carry the sites, so the table is a summary and no implementer would build the wrong thing. Term note: :465 now says "dependent requires checks", but :394 ("typed-access concept probe") and :620 ("uniform-access concept") still call page_supports_uniform_kv_access a concept; it is a constexpr bool variable template (t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:104-108).
