source re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation asked the row to name the two kernel functions and the four rejections (QK rejects a packed-V view and a raw bf16 pointer; PV rejects a native-K view and a raw bf16 pointer), to pair them with positive checks, to write them as dependent requires-expression constants next to the existing constants, and to assert them in the case 'attention operations resolve to typed KV slots'. The row now does all of this [design-r4.txt:465]: 'In namespace tron::amx_attn_h128g4, qk_rowmajor_128x4 must reject raw bf16* / const bf16* and packed V. weights_times_v_128x4 must reject raw pointers and const_native_k_view. Positive checks accept each function's own view.' with 'Place dependent requires checks beside the existing constants at t_llama_unit.cpp:84-123. Assert them in the existing case at 316-342.' Facts verified: the namespace is tron::amx_attn_h128g4 [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@2880c3aa9b:114, :240]; both declarations are unconditional (the header has no #if line at all) [amx_attn_iface.hpp@2880c3aa9b:219-222, :230-233]; the requires-expression constants sit at t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:84-123 and the case at :316 with its STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE block ending at :342. The rejections follow from the design's own contracts: const_view's pointer constructor is explicit [view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:296], so a bf16* or const bf16* is not an implicit argument for the const_native_k_view parameter; packed views expose no pointer constructor or conversion [design-r4.txt:259], so raw pointers are rejected at weights_times_v_128x4; no conversion exists between v_vnni_view and const_view [design-r4.txt:259, :290]. 'Dependent' is the right nuance: a non-dependent requires-expression with an invalid expression is ill-formed, while a variable template on the plane type yields false. The section-9 row [design-r4.txt:570] states both rejection pairs and matches the body; its link [Typed boundary checks] -> #tests resolves. Two notes, no change required: (a) the design does not say how the kernel declarations reach t_llama_unit; they already do, through t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:66 (#include tron/models/model.hpp) -> model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:53 (#include self_attention.hpp) -> self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:21 (#include tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp, unconditional), so no include change is needed and the design's silence is correct; (b) the section-9 M03 row [design-r4.txt:620] does not repeat the two kernel sites that one source-lens verifier asked to be mirrored there; the G30 row directly above it carries them, so the table and body agree. Correction: To the round-3 M03 re-grader corrections (source and fairness lenses), not to the design: the claim that t_llama_unit 'does not include amx_attn_iface.hpp today' is true only for a direct include. The declarations reach it transitively and unconditionally: t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:66 -> h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:53 -> h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:21 -> h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp (no #if in that header). A STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE on the kernel call therefore does not pass for the wrong reason, and the design need not add an include.

Line :190 is the PV counterpart inside "AMX PV stays inside the AVX weight-rounding envelope" (:187-188). Both cases return right after the WARN. So "both QK and PV precision cases" and "AMX unavailable on this host warnings" are right. (2) Child case. t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@30c4ac82cb:188 is the case "AMX QK from the VNNI K plane is bit-identical to AMX QK from row-major K", with WARN("AMX unavailable on this host - VNNI QK identity check skipped") at :200; the QK and PV WARNs are at :147 and :248. (3) Control run. src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@2880c3aa9b:61-62 reads TRON_AMX_DISABLE inside detect_and_request and returns false when it is exactly "1". Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:259 "Owners, views, and rows expose no public raw-pointer constructor, data member, or pointer conversion. Only matrix views construct rows from storage. Same-type row copying is allowed. Rows have no cross-constness conversion. Obtain a read-only row from a read-only matrix view." design-r4.txt:465 "Use STATIC_REQUIRE / STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE for those call contracts, read-only writes, const-row mutation, reverse matrix const conversion, and rvalue-owner views. Reject raw-pointer construction of packed matrices and rows. Accept writable-to-read-only matrix conversion only. Keep explicit native-view pointer construction legal." design-r4.txt:251 "A row stores its pair address and parity by value." Section 9: design-r4.txt:608 "| N14 N20 N22 N50 | Use explicit native-K strides in a declarations header. Restrict row construction. ..."

Checker assessment: The STILL NEEDED text had three parts. (1) One clause at the contract row choosing row conversion or no row conversion: :259 adds "Rows have no cross-constness conversion. Obtain a read-only row from a read-only matrix view." (2) Say in the section-8 row that the accepted writable-to-read-only conversion is between views: :465 says "Accept writable-to-read-only matrix conversion only." (3) A compile-time test of the private-constructor rule for both the view and the row: :465 puts "Reject raw-pointer construction of packed matrices and rows" inside the list of STATIC_REQUIRE / STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE checks. The exact expression the re-grader spelled (STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_constructible_v<v_vnni_row<bf16, D>, bf16*, bool>) and the view form) is not written out, but the design names the macro, the two types and the operation to reject, and :251 gives the row constructor's argument shape (pair address, parity), so an implementer can write the assertion without guessing. The word diff shows the row clause and the rejection sentence are round-4 additions [design-wdiff.txt:183-186; design-r3.txt:438 had neither]. Facts checked. std::is_constructible honours access, so the rejection can be asserted at compile time with a private constructor: a g++ 11.4.0 -std=c++20 probe (scratchpad agent-notes/b04/c_private_ctor.cpp) compiles static_assert(!std::is_constructible_v<v_vnni_row<bf16, 128>, bf16*, bool>), static_assert(!std::is_constructible_v<v_vnni_row<bf16, 128>, bf16*>) and static_assert(!std::is_constructible_v<v_vnni_view<bf16, 64, 128>, bf16*>) with private constructors and a friend declaration from the view. Ben's sketch keeps the view constructor private and states the purpose ("The private constructor prevents routine callers from relabelling an arbitrary row-major pointer as packed data") [comment 5765866077 body lines 86, 97], so the design's row rule extends the reviewer's rule as the round-2 finding asked. The other parts of the original N20 recommendation (private row constructor, matrix view as the only producer, no exposed pointer) were already graded present in round 3 and remain at :259.

Checker assessment: The STILL NEEDED text asked to replace "Within each 16-token by 32-dimension panel, K uses transposed packing." with a sentence that names s = dimension / 32 and c = token / 16, gives the panel base (s * (R / 16) + c) * 512, says the in-panel offset equals the packed-V formula on a 32-row by 16-column plane with row = dimension % 32 and column = token % 16, and spells that offset out; it also called the panel one AMX B tile. Facts checked against the child: k_vnni::index returns (((s * TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 + c) * STEP_PAIRS_16 + dp) * BLOCK_TOKENS_16 + t) * PAIR_2 + j with dp = (dim % 32) / 2, t = token % 16, j = dim % 2 [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:101-107]. Expanding: (s * 4 + c) * 512 + dp * 32 + 2 * t + j. With TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 = R / 16 for R = 64 tokens, that is the design's base plus in-panel offset. The packed-V formula (token / 2) * (2 * D) + 2 * dimension + token % 2 [design-r4.txt:219] with token -> row = dimension % 32, dimension -> column = token % 16 and D = 16 columns gives ((dimension % 32) / 2) * 32 + 2 * (token % 16) + dimension % 2, matching :222. A panel is 16 pair rows x 16 tokens x 2 bf16 = 1,024 bytes = 16 rows of 64 bytes; the child comment says "The pair rows dp = 0..15 of that panel follow at 64-byte steps" [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:110-111]. That is one AMX tile in the VNNI B-operand form (pairs of consecutive dimensions per token column), so "one AMX B tile" is RIGHT. The order prose "dimension groups are outermost and token blocks are next" matches s outermost, c next. Child-only scope is in the table cell :220 "PR #4424 only." The section-9 residual row :594 now links #mapping (HTML line 506), the section that changed, which also settles the fairness-lens link remark. fairness re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation gave the design two options: adopt the guard move, or keep the fakes unconditional and say why in one sentence, while keeping the sentence that amx_attn_iface.hpp includes kv_cache_fwd.hpp. The design declines the move with a stated reason: "These fake bodies are unused when AMX is disabled. Keep their current placement to avoid an extra test refactor." [design-r4.txt:296]. The reason is a design choice, not a factual claim, so it is acceptable under the fairness lens. The both-widths rule stays consistent at every site the finding named: step 1 [design-r4.txt:389], the child paragraph [design-r4.txt:441], the AMX-on row "Compile real kernels and unconditional fake definitions" [design-r4.txt:480], and the 8-lane row keeps the t_amx_dispatch_dtype baseline/head comparison [design-r4.txt:481], which the intent-lens correction (c) asked to keep. The include sentence stays: "amx_attn_iface.hpp includes kv_cache_fwd.hpp and remains free of intrinsics" [design-r4.txt:299]. Every checkable fact is right. The fake definitions sit at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:166-190, outside the #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH that starts at :192; the only TEST_CASE that calls them is under that #ifdef (:192-209), and the AMX-off branch is the placeholder at :210-214. So "unused when AMX is disabled" holds. Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:482 "| NaN-preserving Debug check, 16 lanes | cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug | After this configure command in a fresh worktree, run cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit . Run gen/t_llama_unit with the conversion-case filters. Verify CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug in gen/CMakeCache.txt and absence of -DTRON_IGNORE_NAN in that test's translation-unit entries in gen/compile_commands.json . Make's configuration stamp does not track BUILD_TYPE . Do not use a Make variable change to switch an existing tree. This checks the alternative conversion policy; it is separate from the required Nix production configuration. |" | design-r4.txt:476 "Use a separate worktree for each baseline/head and configuration pair, with the normal gen/ build directory in each. Record compiler version, build type, flags, and generated compile definitions. Presets can accept a different -B directory, but repository Make targets hardcode gen/ and may reconfigure it. Confirm the cached feature values after invoking them. [S17]" | S17 [Make test configuration] link to GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b#L538-L543 (design-r4-links.tsv:464) | section 9 design-r4.txt:569 "Build Debug conversion checks in a separate configured worktree. Use cmake --build and a case filter. Explain the Make configuration stamp and inspect the compiled NaN policy."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation (intent lens, with the design-text and source lenses agreeing) asked the Debug row to: state that Make's configure step does not track BUILD_TYPE; restrict make BUILD_TYPE=Debug to a fresh worktree or drop it; run gen/t_llama_unit with a Catch2 case name instead of make t_llama_unit; confirm -DTRON_IGNORE_NAN is absent from gen/compile_commands.json; confirm CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug in gen/CMakeCache.txt; and remove or qualify "Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo". The new row does all of this. It drops the make BUILD_TYPE=Debug path and the "Plain Make defaults" sentence (both present at design-r3.txt:455, absent at design-r4.txt:482), prescribes cmake --build plus gen/t_llama_unit with filters, states the stamp fact, forbids switching an existing tree through a Make variable, and requires both checks. Checked facts: (1) GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:80 BUILD_TYPE := RelWithDebInfo; the gen/config/test rule at :538-543 depends on $(CMAKELISTS), config/models.yaml, t/proxy/ctest-trampoline.sh, $(FUSE_STATS_STAMP), $(PRESET_STAMP) and the plugin-bundle stamps, and runs cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) ...; the FUSE stamp tracks ENABLE_FUSE_STATS (:289-290) and the preset stamp tracks CMAKE_PRESET (:299-303). No stamp or prerequisite tracks BUILD_TYPE, so "Make's configuration stamp does not track BUILD_TYPE" is right. (2) :880-881 gen/t_%: gen/config/test $(HEADERS) $(SOURCES) runs cmake --build; :886-887 t_%: gen/t_% runs gen/$@ with no arguments, so running gen/t_llama_unit directly with filters is the right way to select cases. (3) TRON_IGNORE_NAN is passed as the compile option -DTRON_IGNORE_NAN under $<NOT:$<CONFIG:Debug>> (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295 and :314-318), so it is absent from Debug compile lines and visible in compile_commands.json; CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS is "1" in the base-ninja preset (CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:22), which the native preset inherits (:31-39, binaryDir gen, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE RelWithDebInfo). (4) CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY is CMAKE_BINARY_DIR (CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:66) and add_catch_test calls add_executable("${TEST_NAME}" ...) (t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:189), so the target name t_llama_unit and the path gen/t_llama_unit are right. (5) The S17 link [Make test configuration] points at GNUmakefile#L538-L543, the gen/config/test rule. Right. Two parts of the corrected text are not repeated: the list of inputs that trigger a reconfigure (CMakeLists.txt, models.yaml, preset input) and the note that make t_<name> runs the whole binary. Neither is load-bearing now: the row no longer uses any Make target, :476 warns that Make targets may reconfigure gen/, and the CMakeCache.txt check catches a reconfigure before the run. Small wording note, no change needed: the cache file line is CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE:STRING=Debug; the row's "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug" is a readable paraphrase.

source re-grader (Resolved): The verifier-merged recommendation asked the Debug row for: a fresh worktree configured with the row's cmake line; a build with cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit; a run of gen/t_llama_unit with a Catch2 case filter (because make t_<name> runs the whole binary unfiltered); a statement that Make's configure step does not track BUILD_TYPE and must not be used to switch an existing gen/; removal or qualification of "Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo"; and a check that -DTRON_IGNORE_NAN is absent from the test's translation-unit entries in gen/compile_commands.json (plus CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug in CMakeCache.txt). design-r4.txt:482 does all of this: "After this configure command in a fresh worktree, run cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit. Run gen/t_llama_unit with the conversion-case filters. Verify CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug in gen/CMakeCache.txt and absence of -DTRON_IGNORE_NAN in that test's translation-unit entries in gen/compile_commands.json. Make's configuration stamp does not track BUILD_TYPE. Do not use a Make variable change to switch an existing tree." The two round-3 sentences ("make BUILD_TYPE=Debug" and "Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo") are gone: 0 hits in the design HTML; the word diff shows them only in an OLD segment [design-wdiff.txt:420]. The facts hold. GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:80 sets BUILD_TYPE := RelWithDebInfo. The configure target gen/config/test at :538-543 depends on $(CMAKELISTS), config/models.yaml, t/proxy/ctest-trampoline.sh, the FUSE stamp (:289-290, tracks ENABLE_FUSE_STATS), the preset stamp (:299-303, tracks CMAKE_PRESET) and the plugin-bundle stamps; none tracks BUILD_TYPE, and the recipe passes -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) at :541. gen/t_%: at :880-881 runs cmake --build gen --target; t_%: at :887-888 runs gen/$@ with no arguments (whole binary, no filter). GNUmakefile is byte-identical at live main (same blob 4a8298f6). CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:22 sets CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS to "1" in base-ninja, which native inherits (:35) with binaryDir gen (:34), so gen/compile_commands.json exists; a command-line -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug overrides the preset's RelWithDebInfo (:37). src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295 and :314-318 add -DTRON_IGNORE_NAN only under $<NOT:$<CONFIG:Debug>> on PUBLIC and INTERFACE compile options, so the t_llama_unit translation-unit entry carries the macro in RelWithDebInfo and lacks it in Debug: the design's check discriminates the two policies. The S17 link "[Make test configuration]" points at GNUmakefile#L538-L543 at 2880c3aa9b [design-r4-links.tsv:464], the configure recipe. Section 9 [design-r4.txt:569] matches the body. Correction: Notes only. (1) "Make's configuration stamp" is shorthand: the configure step is the Make target gen/config/test, whose prerequisites are the stamp files; neither the prerequisites nor the stamps track BUILD_TYPE, so the sentence is right under either reading. (2) The design does not spell out the specific hazard that a plain make target in a hand-configured Debug worktree re-runs cmake with RelWithDebInfo; :476's "may reconfigure it. Confirm the cached feature values" plus the row's CMakeCache.txt check cover it, and the round-3 design-text lens accepted that coverage. Checker's evidence quotes verified at :482, :476, :569 and design-r4-links.tsv:464.

Resolved G42. Uniform-array rule: the 'existing uniform accessor' justification holds only for uniform reclaimability (round 3, grade Note)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r4.txt:366 "For uniform geometry, construct one array over the just-allocated arena's complete contiguous block region. Its bound is the checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t). Construct each arena separately. Uniform geometry with mixed retention still has two arenas. Use the arena pointer just installed by allocate_kv_group, not kv_blocks_alias, which is refreshed later. Both initial allocation and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage use this path." design-r4.txt:562 (section 9) "... Construct each arena separately. Use the arena pointer installed by allocation. Explain uniform geometry with mixed retention without relying on the uniform-reclaimability accessor. [Arena construction]". design-wdiff.txt:280-291: OLD "This matches the existing uniform accessor's indexing across slots." replaced by the four new sentences.

Checker assessment: The justification sentence that the finding targeted is gone. Its replacement narrows the claim to the branch it describes and adds the three clauses of the lead's recommendation (each arena separately, mixed retention has two arenas, arena pointer not kv_blocks_alias). Facts checked. (1) "Cross-slot array indexing exists only in the uniform-reclaimability accessor": kv_block() at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1276-1300 requires uniform_geometry; its uniform_reclaimability branch (:1284-1289) indexes blocks[(slot.i * n_kv_heads + kv_head) * n_pages + pg] from kv_blocks_alias; the else branch (:1290-1299) uses slot_base(kv_storage_offset(physical_slot)) and blocks[kv_head * n_pages + pg]; kv_block_at_storage (:1309-1335) also goes through slot_base. git grep at 2880c3aa9b for "slot.i * n_kv_heads" in kv_cache.hpp hits only :1289. RIGHT. (2) "Uniform geometry with mixed retention still has two arenas": t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:602-622 TEST_CASE "uniform-geometry mixed retention addresses both arenas" frees and restores the reclaimable arena of uniform_mixed_retention_cache while slot 0 keeps its value. RIGHT. (3) "Construct each arena separately" and "Use the arena pointer just installed by allocate_kv_group": allocate_kv_group (:1199-1208) allocates one arena per call and moves it into retained_data or reclaimable_data; it is called at :1101, :1102 and :968. RIGHT. (4) "not kv_blocks_alias, which is refreshed later": refresh_kv_blocks_alias (:1222-1228) sets kv_blocks_alias = slot_base(storage_view_offset_) and is called at :1114 after both constructor allocations and at :971 after the restore allocation at :968. RIGHT. Two of the three round-3 verifiers said this sentence could be dropped because the design never named kv_blocks_alias; keeping it as a caution is correct and harmless. (5) The one-array bound: sizeof(kv_block_t) equals KV_BLOCK_PLANES_2 * page_size * head_size * sizeof(bf16) (:1316-1318), and each slot contributes n_kv_heads * block_bytes per page (:664-666), so every arena byte count is a whole number of blocks. RIGHT. (6) Link: S21 [Uniform and mixed-retention access] kv_cache.hpp#L1285-L1299 at 2880c3aa9b (design-r4-links.tsv, design-r4.txt:675). Optional items the corrections offered that the design did not adopt: no citation of t_llama_unit.cpp:603; no sentence giving the reason the rule holds per arena (identical kv_block_t packed contiguously); the section-8 storage row (design-r4.txt:468) names "mixed geometry" and "release/restore" but not "mixed retention". The lead's final grade was note and the lead's recommended-edits list (r3-findings.md:21-31) does not include G42, so these are not residuals.

In copy_storage_slot , replace the whole-page K memcpy at child kv_cache.hpp:2107 with dst_block.k = src_block.k in the packed branch. Use defaulted owner assignment, as for V. Require ... a 16,384-byte owner for 64 tokens by 128 dimensions." design-r4.txt:470 (section 8, Child only row) "Check masks, independent source rows, whole-plane owner copy, and scratch use." design-r4.txt:443 "Copy the trivially copyable owner's bytes to a test buffer for physical-layout comparisons." Section 9: :574 "Use the defaulted K owner assignment for copy_storage_slot's full-page copy. Use typed token copy for partial pages. Match the V whole-plane owner-copy rule."; :597 (C07) "Use defaulted whole-plane owner copies."

Checker assessment: The design adopts recommendation option 1 with the source-lens narrowing to the packed branch. Facts checked in h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb: copy_storage_slot spans 2093-2141. Line 2099 is if constexpr (k_vnni::layout_on<geometry.head_size>). Line 2106 is the guard src_begin == 0 && dst_begin == 0 && count == page_size. Line 2107 is memcpy(dst_block.k, src_block.k, sizeof(dst_block.k)). So the function name, the line number, and "whole-page" are right. src_block is declared auto const& (2103-2104) and dst_block auto& (2105), so dst_block.k = src_block.k is the defaulted copy assignment from a const owner, which the trivially copyable owner of :428 permits. The token loop at 2109-2115 (k_vnni::gather_row then k_vnni::scatter_row) is what "typed K token copies" replaces. The native branch at 2117-2126 is unchanged by the fix, as asked. Section 8 changed "typed whole-plane copy" (design-r3.txt:443) to "whole-plane owner copy" (:470), as asked. The intent lens also proposed one optional sentence saying the PR body's "Page copies move whole pages with one memcpy" (github-review.json PR body) is preserved by the defaulted copy of the 16,384-byte owner. The design does not add it. The lead note did not require it, and :574 requires verifying the generated copying code, so I do not count it as a residual.

New defect raised by the checker (note): Claim: "Retain the existing array copy in the native branch" (design-r4.txt:434) describes the native branch as an array copy. The native branch at h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2118-2126 computes k_size = geometry.head_size * sizeof(bf16), takes k_at(src_begin).data and k_at(dst_begin).data, and runs memcpy(dst, src, count * k_size). It copies count token rows starting at the given offsets, not the K array. The word "existing" anchors the meaning, so an implementer is unlikely to replace it with a whole-array assignment. Recommendation: write "Retain the existing row-range memcpy in the native branch."

source re-grader (Resolved): The row at design-r4.txt:434 now names the caller, the site and the mechanism: "In copy_storage_slot, replace the whole-page K memcpy at child kv_cache.hpp:2107 with dst_block.k = src_block.k in the packed branch. Use defaulted owner assignment, as for V. Retain the existing array copy in the native branch. Add no K plane-copy helper." [design-wdiff.txt:393-397]. Verified at the child: kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2107 is memcpy(dst_block.k, src_block.k, sizeof(dst_block.k)), inside the if constexpr (k_vnni::layout_on<geometry.head_size>) branch at :2099 and under the full-page guard if (src_begin == 0 && dst_begin == 0 && count == page_size) at :2106; the native branch keeps its k_at().data memcpy at :2118-2126. dst_block is a non-const reference (:2105) and src_block a const reference (:2103-2104), so the defaulted copy assignment of the owner, which :428 requires to be trivially copyable (16,384 bytes for 64 tokens by 128 dimensions), compiles as written. The second requested edit is done: section 8 :470 now says "whole-plane owner copy" instead of "typed whole-plane copy". :416 ("Whole-plane copying uses the defaulted owner assignment described below") and :443 (copy the owner's bytes to a test buffer) are consistent with it, and section 9 :574 matches the body. Because the named K plane-copy operation is removed, the alternative requirement to state a reason for it does not apply.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The design adopted the first offered fix. The row now says: "Use typed K token copies. In copy_storage_slot, replace the whole-page K memcpy at child kv_cache.hpp:2107 with dst_block.k = src_block.k in the packed branch. Use defaulted owner assignment, as for V. The reason for the prefix is stated: "The v_ prefix distinguishes them from the child's k_vnni_* types" [design-r4.txt:55]. Section 9 says "Use parallel v_vnni.hpp and k_vnni.hpp names" and "Parallel filenames are this proposal, not reviewer approval" [design-r4.txt:604]. All header mentions are consistent (v_vnni.hpp at :260, :271, :299, :379, :380, :389, :407, :560, :604). Per the round-4 TRAPS, choosing either offered option with the reason stated resolves the item. Both names compile because tron includes are path-qualified, which round 2 already accepted.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The STILL NEEDED text after round 3 gave two options: revert the V header to h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp at every mention, or add one clause at the child bullet: 'The reviewer's sketch names h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp for both layouts; the two-file split and the v_ prefix are this design's choice.' The design chose the clause and states the reason. design-r4.txt:416: 'The reviewer's sketch used one header, h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp, for both layouts. The separate K/V files and the v_ prefix are this design's choice.' The Words table also gives the naming reason: 'The v_ prefix distinguishes them from the child's k_vnni_* types' [design-r4.txt:55 area, Proposed V types row]. The fact is right: Ben's comment 5765866077 heads its code block '// h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp' and holds both k_vnni_layout and v_vnni_layout [github-review.json]. The corrected round-2 recommendation said no change was required, so the design owed at most this attribution; the round-3 fairness correction asked only that the choice be stated as the design's own, and :416 does that in the body, not only in the section-9 row [design-r4.txt:604 'Parallel filenames are this proposal, not reviewer approval']. The two-file split itself is consistent with round 2, which accepted separate V and K tensor headers. The basename collision between h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp and h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp remains and compiles because tron includes are path-qualified; the design distinguishes the two by full path everywhere it names them [design-r4.txt:62, :299, :416, :417]. Correction: None to the checker's evidence. Grading note for the report: this item was a NOTE with 'no change required' after the round-2 correction; the grade 'resolved' means the design now states its optional deviation and its reason, which is what the STILL NEEDED text asked, not that the deviation was ever a defect.

Major J01. Draft parent runs no Test host job; the required execution evidence has no stated route

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. Source: the three jobs Build ingest, Build model traces and Prepare Tron build inputs each carry if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || !github.event.pull_request.draft || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'Run CI') [.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:168-171, 294-297, 382-385]. Build Tron needs Prepare Tron build inputs [:443]. Test host needs Build Tron [:534]. Test needs all three and requires tron-build success [:663-664]. The header Note says "Draft PRs run lint, machinery, and fresh-plan checks; Run CI enables the product pipeline" [:3-9]. The pull_request trigger lists ready_for_review [:14]. Live evidence agrees: PR 4424 is draft with the single label Skip benchmarks and has no ready_for_review or convert_to_draft event in its timeline (gh, read-only, 2026-09-22). Its GCP Nix run 35046296975 (head ff680c8020, Lint success) skipped Build ingest, Build model traces, Prepare Tron build inputs, Build Tron, Test host, Test FPGA and Test. Non-draft PR 4505 (run 35552493475) ran every one of those jobs including Test host. The design's quoted sentences are exact: the Run CI prohibition [design-r4.txt:167, 495], the evidence rule [:495-497], the completion condition [:535] and the "Before leaving draft" gate [:536]. The design never mentions the draft filter or the ready_for_review trigger (grep: "draft" appears only at :114, :167, :413, :422, :536; "ready_for_review" nowhere; "Run CI" only as a prohibition). AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:12-13 permits ready-for-review for the PR based on main; :17-18 forbids Run CI without direction; :22-28 is the test policy. README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:29 describes Run CI as "Runs draft-gated jobs in default CI ... Do not add unless explicitly directed". N36 [r2-findings.md:487-497] is about the passage marker, F16 about the AMX build in required CI; no round-1 to round-3 facts file or finding mentions pull_request.draft, so this is new evidence. The recommendation's commands exist: make list-tests [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:972-974], bin/slice build-targets --filter=host --build-dir=gen [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:6496-6510], the host filter excludes only fpga-labelled tests [bin/slice:1398], t_llama_unit is registered with LABELS fake [t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:586-592], and the CI runner is bin/slice run --filter=host [nix/tron-test-environment.nix@2880c3aa9b:31-34]. Severity: minor, not major. The route is derivable from rules the design itself states (:167 repeats the stack rule verbatim), the design already names two fallbacks (a user exception at :495, a user-directed rerun at :497), and the parent must leave draft to merge, at which point the full pipeline runs. An implementer would not build the wrong thing and the parent could still merge. The round-3 precedent G22 (a permitted route was derivable; the gap was which route) was graded minor. The text should still change: section 8 explains the second gate (passage marker) in detail and omits the first gate (draft filter), and the pairing of "before committing" (:495) with "before leaving draft" (:536) sends an agent looking for evidence that cannot exist yet.
    Correction: Three narrowings. (1) Citation: design-r4.txt:485 is a blank line and the build-configuration table (:474-482) says nothing about draft state; the only "Before leaving draft" sentence is :536. Cite ":536" alone for that gate and drop ":485" from the section list. (2) The sub-claim "The design also names no local way to verify 'collection'" overstates. The design does name make test-host at :514. That target runs bin/slice run --filter=host --exclude-tag=slow [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:905-906], the same host filter the CI runner uses [nix/tron-test-environment.nix@2880c3aa9b:31-34] minus slow-tagged tests. Reword to: "The design names make test-host (:514) but does not say that it applies the CI runner's host filter, and :495 declares local success insufficient, so the implementer is not told that a local host-filter run or make list-tests is the collection check." (3) The recommendation's sentence "Required execution evidence for the parent therefore exists only after the parent is marked ready for review ... or after a user-directed Run CI label" should add the third route the workflow allows: a user-directed gh workflow run gcp-nix.yml --ref <parent-branch> also passes the filter because github.event_name != 'pull_request' [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:17-20, 168-169], but the design's own rule at :498 counts manual dispatch results as separate evidence, not required PR coverage, so name it only to exclude it. Keep the rest of the recommendation as written; every command and line it cites is verified above. Add the live evidence to the finding's evidence list: PR 4424 run 35046296975 (Lint success, Test host skipped) versus PR 4505 run 35552493475 (Test host ran).
  • design-text lens: holds (high confidence, severity major). The omission is real. The design never says that the GCP Nix product pipeline is draft-gated. The word "draft" appears in the CI context only at design-r4.txt:167, :413, :422, :480 and :536, and none of those lines says that Test host does not run for a draft. The design's five gcp-nix.yml links point at lines 224-237, 486-489, 535-588, 538-590 and 675-698 (design-r4-links.tsv); none covers the draft filter. The filter itself is verified: .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:3-9 (Note [Draft PR Filtering and Label Override], "Draft PRs run lint, machinery, and fresh-plan checks; Run CI enables the product pipeline"), :14 (pull_request types include ready_for_review), :168-171, :294-297 and :382-385 (the if: on Build ingest, Build model traces and Prepare Tron build inputs), :443 (Build Tron needs prepare-tron-build-inputs), :534 (Test host needs tron-build), :601 (Test FPGA needs tron-build), :664 (Test needs tron-build). README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:29 repeats the rule ("Run CI | Runs draft-gated jobs in default CI"). So a draft parent without Run CI has no Test host job. The design demands CI execution evidence before committing a new test (design-r4.txt:495, "Local success alone is insufficient"), requires a Test host run URL (:494), forbids Run CI without user direction (:167, :422, :495), and puts gates "before leaving draft" (:480, :536), but never states that the evidence exists only after ready-for-review or a user-directed label. The passage-marker paragraph (:496) covers a Test host job with skipped steps, not an absent job. AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:12-13 permits the main-based PR to become ready for review and :22-28 forbids agents from deciding an exception, so the implementer has no stated route. The text at :495 is unchanged from round 3 (design-r3.txt:468); no earlier finding raised the draft filter (r1/r2/r3 findings grep "draft" shows only issue-draft and stack items; N36 covers the marker, F16 the AMX build owner). Severity major: a mandatory repository rule cannot be satisfied by an implementer following the page as written without stopping or breaching a rule; one added paragraph fixes it.
    Correction: Narrow three points. (1) The claim "It can exist only after ready-for-review or a Run CI label" omits a third mechanism: gcp-nix.yml has a workflow_dispatch trigger (gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:17-22), and the product jobs' if: passes when github.event_name != 'pull_request' (:168-171), so a user-directed gh workflow run gcp-nix.yml --ref <parent-branch> produces a Test host run at the same source. That run is not attached to the PR as a required check, and the design's own rule at design-r4.txt:497 treats manual dispatch results as "separate evidence, not required PR coverage". Reword to: "Required execution evidence attached to the PR exists only after ready-for-review or a user-directed Run CI label; a user-directed dispatch of gcp-nix.yml proves collection and execution at the same source but is separate evidence under :497." (2) The claim "The design also names no local way to verify collection" is too strong. The design names make test-host (design-r4.txt:514) and links the run-tron-tests skill (:512), whose test-registration entry lists make list-tests (.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:61-62). make test-host runs bin/slice run --filter=host --exclude-tag=slow (GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:905-906), the same filter as the required tron-test-host runner minus slow-tagged tests (nix/tron-test-environment.nix@2880c3aa9b:31-34). Reword to: "The design does not connect make test-host or make list-tests to the AGENTS.md collection check, and does not say that CI execution evidence cannot exist while the parent is draft." (3) Add one precision to the recommendation: a GitHub rerun of a draft run does not create the Test host job either, because the job if: is re-evaluated against the same draft event payload and label changes take effect only on the next PR update (gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:6-7). So the sentence at design-r4.txt:496 "A user-directed GitHub rerun also executes the tests" holds only once the Test host job exists. The rest of the recommendation stands: name the draft gate after :495, state the ready-for-review route as permitted by the stack rule (AGENTS.md:12-13), change :536 to "Before marking the parent ready for review", and tie :535 to the first GCP Nix run after ready-for-review or a user-directed Run CI run.
  • intent lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The GCP Nix product pipeline is skipped for a draft pull request without the Run CI label. Build ingest, Build model traces and Prepare Tron build inputs each carry the condition github.event_name != 'pull_request' || !github.event.pull_request.draft || contains(... 'Run CI') [.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:168-171, 294-297, 382-385; Note at :3-9]. Build Tron needs Prepare Tron build inputs and has no if: of its own [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:443-445]. Test host and Test FPGA need Build Tron [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:534-536, 599-601]. So a draft parent gets no Test host job. README.ci.md confirms this reading: Run CI "Runs draft-gated jobs in default CI" [README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:29]. The design requires required-suite execution evidence [design-r4.txt:495, :496, :535] and forbids Run CI without user direction [design-r4.txt:167, :495]. The design never mentions the draft filter or the ready_for_review trigger [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:14]; a grep of design-r4.txt for draft, ready for review, and Run CI returns only :167, :413, :422, :495. No earlier round raised the draft filter; the only related earlier text is the stack-rule citation in round 1 (r1-findings.md:199) and N36 on marker reuse (r2-findings.md:487-505). The finding is therefore a real, new omission. Under the intent lens the consequence is small, so the severity is minor, not major. Four reasons. (1) The route to the evidence already exists in the design: :167 says the PR based on main may become ready for review, and the parent is that PR. The ready_for_review event runs the whole pipeline [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:14], and every later push to a non-draft PR does too. The parent must become ready for review before Ben can review or merge it, so the evidence is produced on the normal path without any label. (2) The "before leaving draft" gates at :485 and :536 are local checks: compile the 16-lane AMX-on configuration and run the fake dispatch cases. Required CI does not build AMX at all [design-r4.txt:492], so those gates never depended on CI. The finding wrongly groups them with the CI-evidence problem. (3) The CI-evidence item at :535 is a Definition-of-done bullet, not a pre-ready gate, so its timing (after ready-for-review) is already consistent with the pipeline. The evidence fields at :496 (Test host run URL, attempt, runtime store paths, case names) cannot be filled from a draft run, which has no Test host job, so an agent cannot mistake a draft run's lint-only green for execution evidence. (4) The circular wording "before committing a new test, verify ... execution" is the repository rule's own wording [AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24]; the design restates it and adds nothing false. The realistic harm is an implementing agent stalling or asking jhan for a Run CI label or an exception that is not needed. That is a process cost, not a wrong build and not a blocked merge. A one-sentence clarification removes it, so the text should change, and the risk if it does not is low.
    Correction: Narrow the finding in three places and fix one citation. (a) Section list and claim: drop :485 and :536 from the conflict. Those gates are local (16-lane AMX-on compile plus fake dispatch cases, which required CI never builds [design-r4.txt:492]); keep :167, :494-497 and :535. (b) Replace "cannot obtain the evidence and is told not to use the only label that would produce it" with: "the design does not say that the product jobs are draft-gated, so it does not say that the evidence exists only after the parent is marked ready for review (permitted by :167 and triggered by ready_for_review, gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:14), after a user-directed rerun of such a run (:497), or after a user-directed Run CI label; an agent may stall or ask for an unneeded label or exception." (c) Recommendation: keep the one added sentence after :495 (draft filter, ready-for-review route, citations gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:3-9, 14, 168-171, 294-297, 382-385, 443, 534-536, 599-601). For the local collection check, cite bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:1398 and :3106 (--filter=host selects every registered test whose labels do not include fpga), together with t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:586-592 (t_llama_unit, LABELS fake) and nix/tron-test-environment.nix@2880c3aa9b:31-34 (tron-test-host runs bin/slice run --filter=host); the commands make list-tests [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:972-974] and bin/slice build-targets --build-dir=gen --filter=host [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:360] both exist. Drop the change to :536; "leaving draft" and "marking ready for review" mean the same thing there, and that bullet is a local gate. For :535 add "from a GCP Nix run whose Test host steps executed: the first run after ready-for-review, a user-directed rerun, or a user-directed Run CI run", not "the first run", because :497 already covers marker reuse and reruns. (d) Grade minor: one sentence of text should change; the route is already permitted at :167 and the evidence fields at :496 already prevent a false record.

Minor J03. pair_base names two different functions; the Words row defines only the V meaning

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The Words row defines pair_base once, as the V-pair address [design-r4.txt:49]. The V formula uses that meaning in bf16-element units [design-r4.txt:257]. Both lines are unchanged from round 3 [design-r3.txt:49, :246]. The round-4 text adds a second use: "Move their pair_base, pair_row_offsets, and transpose_16x16_epi32 helpers" into h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp [design-r4.txt:416; design-wdiff.txt REPLACE @old 6348 / new 7703]. That pair_base is the child's detail::pair_base(plane, s, token). It returns a char* byte address [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:113 and :119]. Its comment reads "The byte address of dimension pair 0 of dimension step s for token token. The pair rows dp = 0..15 of that panel follow at 64-byte steps." [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:110-111]. Its body is reinterpret_cast<char*>(plane) + ((s * TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 + c) * PANEL_DWORDS_256 + t) * DWORD_BYTES_4 [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:115-116]. So the two meanings differ in unit (bf16 elements versus bytes), in layout (V token pair versus packed-K panel lane) and in arguments (implicit token versus (plane, s, token)). pair_row_offsets is at :126 and transpose_16x16_epi32 at :153 of the same file, as the finding says. The child's only callers of pair_base are the K helpers [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:144, :225]. Main 2880c3aa9b has no k_vnni.hpp (facts-r4.md:128-129). Severity: minor. The glossary row misdefines a term the design now uses in a second sense, so the text should change. Risk if it does not change is low: the implementer moves the child's code as written, and the child's own comment states the byte-address meaning.
    Correction: Two small narrowings. (1) The child's comment says "dimension step s", not "dimension group s" [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:110]. The design's own layout text says "dimension groups" and "s = dimension / 32" [design-r4.txt:222]. The recommended Words text should use the design's word and give the child's in parentheses: "dimension group s (the child's comment says dimension step)". (2) The recommended citation "k_vnni.hpp:109-180" also spans scatter_row (:135-146), which is not one of the three helpers. Cite the two detail blocks instead: "k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:109-133 (pair_base at :113 and :119, pair_row_offsets at :126) and :148-180 (transpose_16x16_epi32 at :153)". The rest of the recommendation stands.
  • design-text lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The finding's central claim holds. The Words row states one meaning: "pair_base is the address of the first bf16 value of a V token pair" [design-r4.txt:49]. That matches the V formula "pair_base = plane + (token / 2) * 2 * D" in bf16-element units [design-r4.txt:257]. The round-4 text then says "Move their pair_base, pair_row_offsets, and transpose_16x16_epi32 helpers with them" into h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp [design-r4.txt:416]. That sentence is new in this revision [design-wdiff.txt:376-377, REPLACE @old 6348 / new 7703]. The only pair_base in the child is detail::pair_base(bf16* plane, size_t s, size_t token) [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:113, const overload :119]. Its comment reads "The byte address of dimension pair 0 of dimension step s for token token. The pair rows dp = 0..15 of that panel follow at 64-byte steps" [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:110-111]. It returns a char* byte offset ((s * TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 + c) * PANEL_DWORDS_256 + t) * DWORD_BYTES_4 [:115-117]. So the two uses differ in unit, layout and arguments, as the finding says. pair_base occurs in the design only at :49, :257 and :416; no line gives the K meaning or says the name has two meanings. :437 describes the K lane layout without naming pair_base. The Words row is unchanged from round 3 [design-r3.txt:49; design-r3.txt has pair_base only at :49 and :246]. (2) Fix the line range in the recommendation: the child's detail helpers sit in two blocks, :109-133 (pair_base at :113 and :119, pair_row_offsets at :126) and :148-180 (transpose_16x16_epi32 at :153); scatter_row at :139-146 lies between them and is not a detail helper [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb]. Write "(k_vnni.hpp:109-133 and :148-180)" instead of "(k_vnni.hpp:109-180)". (3) Offer the smaller fix as an alternative: instead of a two-meaning Words row, rename the V formula variable at :257 (for example "pair_start") and update :49 to match, or write "the child's detail::pair_base" at :416. Either removes the ambiguity. Also match the design's own vocabulary: the child comment says "dimension step s" [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:110]; the design says "dimension groups" and "s = dimension / 32" [design-r4.txt:222]; the proposed Words text should say "dimension group s (the child's 'dimension step')" so both names resolve.

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The sentence is new in round 4: the round-3 text gave no value [design-r3.txt:257; design-wdiff.txt:234-235]. Consequence for jhan's goal: the sentence contradicts the design's own 'Preserve existing DMA flags' disposition for G41 and N15 [design-r4.txt:573, :609]. No packed body reads the flag [design-r4.txt:252], so there is no runtime effect; this keeps the severity at minor, not major. It is not a note: the design text carries a false statement about a production type that Ben, the author of the tensor sketch, will read, and it conflicts with two disposition rows.

(1) 'Only the host executor yields dma = false' is right, but say why the value appeared: host_bf16 and host_fp16 also carry dma = true (dmatensor<bf16> and dmatensor<fp16> [common.hpp@2880c3aa9b:101-102; btensor.hpp:21; htensor.hpp:8]); the false value is real only for make_llm_executor<false, tensor, tensor, tensor>, which t_llama_unit's model cases use [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:1252, :1298, :1323, :1852, :1986]. Note J08. load_row for float destinations duplicates row.chunk() plus view::set

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The design tells the implementer to write the even/odd extraction twice inside h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp. Sentence one: "Copy the extraction pattern from the existing float get_v loop into v_vnni_row::chunk(): shift left by 16 bits for even tokens and mask with 0xffff0000 for odd tokens" [design-r4.txt:262]. Sentence two: "load_row moves today's get_v loops" [design-r4.txt:272], and load_row's destination is bf16 or float [design-r4.txt:270], so the moved loops include the float loop. Today's float loop is, per 16 dimensions, one _mm512_load_si512, one _mm512_slli_epi32 by 16 (even) or _mm512_and_si512 with 0xffff0000 (odd), and one _mm512_store_ps [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2418-2421, :2427-2430]. The existing rank-1 view::set already composes exactly that from a row expression: view& set(expr<X, d0> const& x) loops chunky<T, aligned>::set(data, i, x.chunk(i)) when s0 == 1 && writeable_in_chunks<T, aligned> [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:188-191, inside the rank-1 specialization at :116]. writeable_in_chunks<float, true> holds because chunky<float, true>::set exists [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp@2880c3aa9b:105-107, :34-36]. That set is tron_mm_store_ps [chunky.hpp:35], which is _mm512_store_ps at 16 lanes [h/tron/simd/auto.hpp@2880c3aa9b:65]. The design's load_row destination is view<Destination, true, Dma, seq<D>, sseq<1>> [design-r4.txt:268], so s0 == 1 and aligned == true, and D is divisible by chunk_size [design-r4.txt:298], so the tail branch of set is discarded. The row inherits expr<row_type, D> [design-r4.txt:251]. So dst.set(src[token]) is well-formed with the design's own types and is the float unpack; a moved float loop is a second copy of the same mechanism. The existing view::set (the tensor-library function that copies a rank-1 expression into a contiguous row) already loops chunky<float,true>::set, which is tron_mm_store_ps [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:187-191; h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp@2880c3aa9b:30-37, :106-108]. The consequence is small, so the severity is lowered to note under the intent lens. Nothing wrong gets built: both copies compute the same values. The parent merges either way. Ben's sketch asks for exactly what the design wrote: "hot paths use the bulk operations below", "Use overloads for the two layouts, rather than a generic scalar loop in the hot path", and "For V, the overloads contain the existing interleave/deinterleave operations, including the required BF16, FP16, and float conversions" [github-review.json, comment 5765866077, section 4]. A float load_row that is a moved loop follows that sentence literally. The finding's fix (load_row calls the generic expression-assignment path) departs from the letter of the sketch. The departure is harmless because the float path has no production caller, but it is not something Ben asked for. Round 3 already recorded this duplication risk: G13's lead recommendation allowed "copy ... or hoist", and its verifier correction asked that chunk(i) "reuse one iteration of the load_row loop". The design chose copy [design-r4.txt:262, :558]. That is a permitted choice, so J08 records a maintainability preference, not a defect that must change before implementation. Two accuracy slips in the finding. First, the quoted sentence "load_row moves today's get_v loops" is at design-r4.txt:272, not :268 (:268 is the declaration line). Second, "the same instructions written twice" over-claims slightly: get_v(float*) hoists the parity test outside its loop and emits two loop bodies [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2419, :2426], while a row expression stores parity by value [design-r4.txt:251] and would test it inside every chunk(i) call. The two match only after the compiler applies loop unswitching (moving a loop-invariant branch outside the loop), which GCC enables at -O3 [design-r4.txt:522 says the build adds -O3]. The finding's own instruction-comparison addition would detect a miss, so this is a narrowing, not a refutation.

Note J14. Native-branch K copy is called an array copy; it is a row-range memcpy

2 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The design row reads exactly as quoted: "Use defaulted owner assignment, as for V. Retain the existing array copy in the native branch. Add no K plane-copy helper." [design-r4.txt:434]. The native branch of copy_storage_slot in the child is the else arm of if constexpr (k_vnni::layout_on<geometry.head_size>) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2099, :2117]. That arm computes constexpr size_t k_size = geometry.head_size * sizeof(bf16);, takes .k_at(src_begin).data and .k_at(dst_begin).data, and runs memcpy(dst, src, count * k_size); [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2119-2126]. It copies count token rows from the given offsets. It does not copy an array. Main has the identical code [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1933-1941]. The packed branch's whole-page copy is memcpy(dst_block.k, src_block.k, sizeof(dst_block.k)) [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2107]. Its partial-range path is the gather_row/scatter_row loop [:2109-2115; the row buffer is :2109, the loop :2110-2115]. Partial ranges are real: copy_from passes arbitrary src_begin, dst_begin and count bounded only by page_size [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2147-2153], and the design preserves "whole-page and partial-page append" [design-r4.txt:468]. The K member in the native branch is the C array alignas(kv_block_alignment) bf16s k[page_size][head_size / chunk_size]; [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2194; child :2380]. The sentence is new in round 4 [design-wdiff.txt:394]; design-r3.txt has no "native branch" or "array copy" text. The round-3 G44 source-lens correction had given the exact wording "the native branch [2118-2126] keeps its row-range memcpy over k_at().data" [r3-findings.md, G44 verifier correction (c)]; the design paraphrased it as "existing array copy". Severity minor: the loose phrase sits directly after the owner-assignment sentence, a one-phrase fix removes the misreading, and the risk if unfixed is low because "Retain the existing" tells the implementer to keep the code that is there.
    Correction: Narrow three details. (1) The design is not silent on the mechanism. Section 6 already says "Preserve native-K and 8-lane V row-range byte copies" [design-r4.txt:376]. The imprecision is local to the section-7 row [:434]. Reword the claim to: "Section 6 [:376] names the native K copy correctly as a row-range byte copy; the section-7 row [:434] calls the same code an 'array copy', which does not match." (2) The "fails to compile" sentence covers only one wrong reading. dst_block.k = src_block.k on the C array is ill-formed, so that reading fails to compile. A whole-array memcpy(dst_block.k, src_block.k, sizeof(dst_block.k)) rewrite would compile and would copy 64 rows for a partial range. "Retain the existing" instructs no rewrite, so the risk stays low. Reword to: "One wrong reading (owner assignment of the C array) fails to compile; a whole-array memcpy rewrite would compile, but 'Retain the existing' forbids a rewrite." (3) The design's own term "array branch" [:428, "Constrain native k_view() and k_at() to the array branch"] gives "array copy" a consistent internal reading (the copy in the array branch). Say so; it lowers the risk further. Recommended replacement sentence for :434: "Retain the native branch's existing row-range memcpy of count rows from k_at(src_begin).data to k_at(dst_begin).data (child kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2117-2127; main 2880c3aa9b:1933-1941), as section 6 [:376] already requires."

Main has the same memcpy [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1933-1941]. The K member is a C array [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2194]. The packed whole-page memcpy is at 2107 [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2107]. The central claim does not hold for an implementer reading the page, for three reasons. (1) The design already states the precise rule the finding says is missing. Section 6 says: "Preserve native-K and 8-lane V row-range byte copies, packed-V token copies in all four parity combinations, page-boundary splitting, overlap restrictions, and completion-state copying." [design-r4.txt:376]. "Row-range byte copies" for native K is exactly the memcpy of count rows the finding describes. Section 7 restates that rule in short form and relies on it. (2) "Array" in the section-7 row is the design's name for the native storage branch, not a statement about the extent of the copy. The storage block calls the native type native_k_storage = bf16s[page_size][head_size / chunk_size] with the comment "Existing array shape is retained for native K" [design-r4.txt:426]. That is the intended and correct reading. The alternative reading, "copy the whole array", requires ignoring both "retain" and "existing". (3) "Retain the existing" is an instruction to leave code unchanged. It cannot direct an implementer to write a different copy. The new sentence "Retain the existing array copy in the native branch" is codex's short form of that. Section 9's G44 row matches the body [design-r4.txt:574].

Optional: reword the row to 'Retain the native branch's existing row-range memcpy of count rows from k_at(src_begin) to k_at(dst_begin) [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2117-2127]' so the row is self-contained." The nearest defined terms are pair_base ("the address of the first bf16 value of a V token pair", :49) and "tile", which Words uses only for the 1024-byte AMX tile ("A packed-K panel contains 16 tokens by 32 dimensions and corresponds to one AMX tile", :49; "one AMX B tile", :222). The source evidence is right: the constructor stores const bf16s* const data as a member [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1992, initialized at :2074] and computes const bf16x32* tile = reinterpret_cast<const bf16x32*>(data + i * (head_size / chunk_size)) inside the per-pair loop [:2084-2085 for head 64, :2099-2100 for head 128] before _mm512_dpbf16_ps(t0, _mm512_load_si512(tile + 0), scale) [:2086, :2101]. page::scaled_v passes kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v[0] [:2261-2262], and v is bf16s v[page_size / 2][head_size / chunk_size * 2] [:2197-2198], so today's data member is the packed plane's first address, as the recommendation says.     Correction: Three corrections. (1) Drop "matches no name in the existing constructor". tile is a local variable of that constructor [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2084, :2099; also :2016 inside accumulate_16_chunks]. Only the compound "pair-tile" and the word "base" match nothing (the member is named data, :1992). (2) Narrow the misreading. The sentence says "obtains ... once", so a per-iteration fetch is not a natural reading. Note J28. Fixture rule forbids the smaller byte-copy route that round-3 G22 left open

2 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity note). The central facts of J28 are right. Round 3 asked the design to state a policy, not to forbid the byte copy: the G22 lead note says "the design should state whether tests may do it rather than the finding forbidding it", and the intent-lens correction says "State whether a memcpy ... is allowed in tests. Prefer the append_v_row route" [r3-findings.md, G22 LEAD NOTE and intent correction; recommended-edit list item 2]. The round-4 text states a prohibition for "these fixtures", gives a one-clause reason, and concedes legality: "Do not copy hand-packed input bytes into the owner in these fixtures. This fixture rule verifies the public typed write path. It is not a claim that byte copying into a trivially copyable owner is illegal C++." [design-r4.txt:401]. The mandated route is 64 appends: "Append all 64 tokens in order with append_v_row through its bf16 input path" [design-r4.txt:399], plus a copy-out and compare [design-r4.txt:401]. The owner is 16,384 bytes [design-r4.txt:398], equal to 64 x 128 x 2 bytes. The existing PV case builds std::vector<tron::bf16> v_page by the pair formula from std::vector<float> v through bf16_rne [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:199, :203-211] and passes v_page.data() to the kernel [:226-227]; its reference reads v_page by the same formula [:238-239]. A memcpy of those 16,384 bytes into a default-constructed, trivially copyable owner followed by owner.as_view() is therefore the smaller edit, and the finding says so as a judgment, not as an error. G22 itself is resolved under the corrected recommendation, because the design now states the policy it was asked to state; J28 is a new note on the choice. Two details are off. (1) The kernel call is at :226-227; :225 is begin_region() [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:225-227]. facts-r4.md carries the same :225-226 slip. (2) "which the t_llama_unit 'V append and padding' row already covers" is true only for the operation's logical effect. That row observes appended V through scaled_v with one-hot scales and poison [design-r4.txt:462; t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:2737-2745, :2806-2812, :1785], and no t_llama_unit case compares raw V storage bytes against an independent pair formula (no memcmp or to_bits pattern check on V storage at 2880c3aa9b). The PV numerics case holds the parent's only independent statement of the physical layout ("the pair-interleaved storage the kernel consumes as-is" [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:197-198, :207]), and weights_times_v_128x4 reads storage directly. So the byte compare the design adds is the one parent check that append_v_row writes the bytes the AMX kernel reads. The design's reason is therefore stronger than J28 grants, and the finding should present the prohibition as a trade of about 15 fixture lines for that check.

The design text does forbid copying hand-packed input bytes into the owner in the numerics fixtures, gives the reason (the fixture verifies the public typed write path), and concedes that the copy is legal C++ [design-r4.txt:401]. The round-3 G22 correction asked the design to "state whether" the memcpy route is allowed and to "prefer the append_v_row route"; it added "the design should choose, not the finder" [r3-findings.md G22, intent-lens correction]. The design chose the preferred route and stated the policy, so G22 is resolved as corrected; section 9 says the same [design-r4.txt:565]. The finding does not dispute that; it argues the design's choice is not the smallest edit. The byte-copy route is indeed shorter: one memcpy of 16,384 bytes plus owner.as_view(), with the hand-packed std::vector at t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203-210, the kernel call at :225-226 and the reference at :238-239 otherwise untouched. The design's route needs one 64-byte-aligned bf16 row buffer, 64 append_v_row calls, a byte copy-out and a compare [design-r4.txt:399-401]. That is a difference of roughly 15 to 20 lines in one test case. Either route gives an implementable parent PR, and PR 4424 rebases onto either. Ben's stated wish is encapsulation: "we really don't want bf16_t* values floating around without any indication of how they are laid out" [github-review.json comments[2], id 5270587330] and "the layout defines the byte mapping; storage owns those bytes" [comments[3], id 5765866077]. A test that injects self-encoded layout bytes into storage is the pattern Ben wants removed from production, so the design's stricter rule is at least as acceptable to Ben as the finding's relaxed rule. jhan's request says another agent implements the design from the file [codex-add-tensor-type.md, "Another agent will implement the design by reading this file"], so one named route is better for the implementer than two permitted routes. Three parts of the finding are also imprecise. (2) "keeps the case's stated purpose ... separate from the write path" under-states the design: the numerical reference still comes from the original logical input, not from the typed view [design-r4.txt:402], so the reference is independent under both routes; only the kernel input passes through append_v_row, and the byte compare against the test's own pair formula isolates a write-path failure [design-r4.txt:401]. (3) The t_llama_unit row covers append_v_row through page::set_v and a weighted sum via page::scaled_v, the AVX-side read path [design-r4.txt:462, :286]; it does not check that append_v_row's bytes match what the AMX kernel weights_times_v_128x4 consumes. The design's route adds that writer-to-kernel layout agreement check inside t_amx_numerics; the byte-copy route would not. So the prohibition has a verification benefit the finding does not weigh. Severity stays note: the design text need not change.

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity note). The central claim holds. The section-9 row says the unconditional fakes give "declaration checking ... in AMX-off builds" [design-r4.txt:559]. In an AMX-off build no code references the kernels, so a fake whose parameter list drifts is an unrelated overload and compiles silently. Facts checked at 2880c3aa9b (identical at live main 0a51385e95 for these files): - Every amx_attn_h128g4 use in self_attention.hpp sits inside an #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH block. The uses are at :265, :1438-1462, :1583-1586, :1634-1680 and :1757. The guarded blocks are :259-267, :1429-1464, :1571-1701 and :1748-1771 [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b]. - amx_attn.cpp is a tron source only under if(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH) [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:219-224]. tron is a STATIC library [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:187]. - The fake definitions are outside any #ifdef; the TEST_CASE is under #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH at :192 [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:166-190, :192-213]. The test links tron and pos_fake [t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:596]. - The compiler warning flags are -Wall -Wpedantic -Wextra -Wno-shadow, plus -Wstrict-overflow for GCC [CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:608-611]. No -Wmissing-declarations and no compiler -Werror exists in CMakeLists.txt, src, t, cmake, nix, flake.nix, CMakePresets.json or GNUmakefile (the two -Werror hits are clang-format calls). - Compile probe in the scratchpad (g++ -std=c++20 with tron's four warning flags): a definition of qk_rowmajor_128x4 whose first parameter is a struct instead of const bf16* compiles with exit 0 and no diagnostic. Because tron is a STATIC library [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:187], the drift surfaces only in an AMX-on link, where the guarded test body calls the declared typed function, the linker pulls amx_attn.o, and its duplicate definitions of available()/begin_region()/etc. collide with the fakes. Third, no implementation consequence: the only harm is that a reader of the disposition table may believe the required Nix lane (16 lanes, AMX off, :479) validates kernel signatures. The finding is partly wrong in saying the benefit "does not exist": see the correction.
    Correction: Narrow the claim in three places. (1) Replace "gives a benefit that does not exist" with "over-states the benefit". The AMX-off compile of the unconditional fakes does check three things against the header: (a) the by-value parameter classes are complete and instantiate at the fixed 64x128 shape in that build (g++: a definition with an incomplete by-value type is an error, a declaration is not; at 8 lanes the fakes are the only instantiation of the packed V view, because the cache uses the packed owner only in 16-lane blocks [design-r4.txt:389]); (b) the return type and the noexcept specifier agree with the declaration (g++ 11.4 errors: "has a different exception specifier", "ambiguating new declaration"); (c) the alias names and constants the fakes spell exist in the header. It does not check that the fake parameter lists match the declarations: a drifted fake is an unused overload, compiled with no warning under -Wall -Wextra. (2) Fix the attribution: the quote "checks nothing extra" is from the round-3 G14 design-text lens correction (c) only [r3-findings.md G14]; the source lens said "not a functional loss, because ... a signature mismatch is only observable with AMX on". Same substance, different words. (3) Reword the recommended replacement for design-r4.txt:559 to: "Keep class definitions complete in both vector widths. The AMX-off compile of the unconditional fakes checks only that their parameter classes are complete and that return type and noexcept match the declarations; a parameter-type drift compiles as an unused overload and surfaces only in an AMX-on link, where the static tron library pulls in the real amx_attn.o. The fakes keep their placement to avoid an extra test refactor [Build boundaries]." Add one observation: the section-9 cell carries a rationale that the body [:296] does not; under this round's rule that a Design response cell counts only if the body carries it, the cell should repeat the body's reason (the test-refactor cost) rather than introduce a new one. Citations: design-r4.txt:296, :389, :479-481, :559; self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b guarded blocks listed in the reason; src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:187, :219-224; t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:39, :166-190, :192-214; t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:594-596 (test registered unconditionally, "Defines CPU fakes for every amx_attn_h128g4 entry point in its own TU"); h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@2880c3aa9b:219-222, :230-233 (declarations under no preprocessor condition).

(a) The generator has exactly two save-call emit sites: "save_k_helper" at ingest/src/TronCpp.hs@30c4ac82cb:2338 and "save_k" at :2406. The design's next instruction, "Both save_k< counts become 2 calls" [design-r4.txt:451], requires both sites to emit outer_state.template save_k<. The text "save_k<" is not a substring of "save_k_helper<". So a leftover helper prefix at either site drops the save_k< count to 1 and fails the retained assertions at :2801 and :3225. The design then lists what happens to each group: two save_k< counts, two save_k_helper< counts, two main-call tails, one helper-call prefix, and the unchanged :3232 [design-r4.txt:451]. That is 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 7 under either reading. "Deleting two of them leaves five edits, not seven" is the finding's own reframing of "affected" as "surviving", which the design does not say. Rejected J38. DoD deferral clause is a user exception to the refresh rule; the drift warning is unnamed

Candidate claim: The new completion bullet permits 'an explicit deferral with user direction' for a materially changed test-cost record. The repository rules have no deferral clause: t/AGENTS.md says to refresh config/test-benchmarks.json after adding or materially changing a test, and the run-tron-tests skill says such tests 'require' bin/slice bench --new or --update. The design should label the deferral as a user exception to those rules, consistent with its own :495 wording for the test-execution rule. The bullet also says only that --check 'detects missing records, not stale timings'. Slice does react to a stale timing: bin/slice run prints 'Drift detected — consider running bin/slice bench:' with the test name when a test's measured duration differs from its record by more than 30 % (DRIFT_TEST_PCT = 0.30) or the run's makespan by more than 20 % (DRIFT_MAKESPAN_PCT = 0.20). This is a warning to stderr, not a failure. Naming it tells the implementer what a deferred refresh looks like in the Test host log.

The skill says "New or materially changed tests require bin/slice bench --new or bin/slice bench --update <name> after the test passes" [.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:69-70]. (2) A drift warning exists and the design never mentions it (grep for "drift" over design-r4.txt returns nothing). DRIFT_TEST_PCT = 0.30 and DRIFT_MAKESPAN_PCT = 0.20 [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:115-116]. emit_drift_warnings prints "Drift detected — consider running bin/slice bench:" plus one line per test to stderr and returns None, so the exit status does not change [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:3022-3048]. cmd_bench_check reports platform-block problems and missing manifest entries only, with no timing comparison [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:1792-1832], so the design's ":537 --check detects missing records, not stale timings" is right. One detail of the finding is wrong. The CI Test host job runs tron-test-host [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:573], which is exec bin/slice run --filter=host with no -v [nix/tron-test-environment.nix@2880c3aa9b:31-34]. make test-host runs bin/slice run $(SLICE_REMOTE_ARGS) --filter=host --exclude-tag=slow with no -v, and SLICE_REMOTE_ARGS carries only --remote options [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:906, :167-175]. So the "Drift detected" line does not appear in the Test host log or in a default make test-host run.   • intent lens: refuted (high confidence, severity note). The finding has two parts. Part 1 (label the deferral as a user exception) is true but has no consequence. Part 2 (name the drift warning as the Test host log symptom) is wrong on its central factual claim, and the recommended text would put an error into the design. Part 1. The repository rules have no deferral clause; that is confirmed. t/AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:23-26 says to refresh config/test-benchmarks.json after adding or materially changing a test. .agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:69-70 says such tests "require" bin/slice bench --new or --update. But the deferral wording in the design is exactly what the round-3 review asked for. The G26 intent-lens correction proposed the bullet text "refreshed on delphi-3bda under user direction, or the deferral and the user's direction are recorded in the PR description" [r3-findings.md, G26 VERIFIER CORRECTION (intent lens)]. The design-text correction proposed the same [r3-findings.md, G26 VERIFIER CORRECTION (design-text lens)]. The design now carries it at design-r4.txt:537 and repeats the user-direction requirement at :515 ("Bench requests the whole host ... so it requires user direction"). Whether the design calls this an "exception" or a "deferral with user direction" changes nothing an implementer does: user direction is required either way, and it is recorded in the PR either way. This part is a wording preference, not a defect that affects jhan's goal (an implementable parent PR that Ben accepts). Part 2. The claim "bin/slice run prints 'Drift detected ...' when a test's measured duration differs from its record by more than 30 %" is true only with the -v/--verbose flag. emit_drift_warnings is called only under if args.verbose: [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:4554-4555]. The run subparser documents the flag as "show per-test (expected Ns) and the end-of-run drift report" [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:6530-6533]. The CI Test host job runs the tron-test-host wrapper [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:573], and that wrapper executes bin/slice run --filter=host with no verbose flag [nix/tron-test-environment.nix@2880c3aa9b:31-34]. make test-host also passes no verbose flag [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:905-906]. So the "Drift detected" line never appears in the Test host log, and the recommendation's sentence "bin/slice run prints 'Drift detected' in the Test host log" is false. The line that always appears is the summary "N passed, N skipped, N failed • makespan Xs expected Ys (speedup Zx)" [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:4545-4550]; it shows the expected total, not a per-test stale record. The design's existing sentence "bin/slice bench --check detects missing records, not stale timings" (design-r4.txt:537) stays correct [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:1792-1832; facts-r4.md]. Nothing in the finding shows an implementer would build the wrong thing or that Ben would object. Severity if the true part held alone: note. The finding is refuted because its only non-duplicate content (the Test host log symptom) is wrong.
